title: feat(site-exporter): self-booting export ZIPs — bundle index.php + readme.txt for fresh-host install
body:
## Summary

Today's export ZIPs (single-site or, after #1149, network-wide) require the target server to already have **WordPress installed**, **WP-CLI available**, and the **Ultimate Multisite plugin active** before the import will work. That is fine for migrating between two managed networks but blocks the most common DR / clone-to-fresh-host use case.

This issue makes export ZIPs **self-booting**: extract the ZIP onto an empty webroot, hit the URL in a browser, follow a 5-minute-install-style wizard, done. The ZIP carries everything needed to install WordPress, install this plugin, and run the bundled import.

## Status

**Blocked by #1149** — needs the network bundle format frozen so the installer knows what it's installing. Single-site self-boot can land first if it's clearer to ship in two PRs (single-site → network), but bundle-format compatibility must be settled in #1149 first.

## Scope (this issue)

Add a self-boot bootstrap to BOTH bundle types (single-site + network):

- At export time, write two new files into the ZIP root:
  - `index.php` — the self-boot installer entry point.
  - `readme.txt` — extraction + import instructions for humans.
- The installer must:
  1. Detect when no `wp-config.php` exists (= fresh extraction → run wizard) vs. when WordPress is already installed (= short-circuit, refuse to run, point user to the standard import flow).
  2. Render an HTML wizard collecting: DB credentials (host, name, user, password, prefix), site URL, admin email, admin password, language. For network bundles: subdomain vs. subdirectory mode (default to whatever the bundle declares in `network.json`).
  3. Acquire WordPress core (see "Core acquisition strategy" below).
  4. Acquire WP-CLI (see same).
  5. Run `wp core install` (single-site bundle) **or** `wp core install` + `wp core multisite-convert` (network bundle).
  6. Install + network-activate this plugin from inside the bundle (the export ZIP includes the plugin source under a known path — implementer to decide whether to bundle a copy or download from the WordPress.org / GitHub release).
  7. Run the bundled importer:
     - Single-site bundle → existing `wu_exporter_import()` path.
     - Network bundle → `wu_exporter_import_network()` from #1150 (Issue B) IF that has shipped, ELSE the equivalent CLI command directly against `network.sql` + `sites/*`.
  8. On success: delete `index.php` + `readme.txt` from the webroot, leave a `wu-bootstrap-complete.log` for audit, redirect to `/wp-admin/`.
  9. On failure: render a clear error page with the failed step, the captured stdout/stderr, and a "Try again" button (idempotent — re-running should resume from the failed step where possible).

## Out of scope

- Multi-network bootstrapping into an existing network (= merge, also out of scope of #1150).
- Downloading paid addons during bootstrap. The bundle has whatever was active at export time; addons not included are not magically restored.
- HTTPS provisioning / DNS setup. The wizard assumes the URL the user types resolves to the server they extracted the ZIP onto.

## Core acquisition strategy

Two viable patterns — implementer should support **both**, with auto-fallback:

| Strategy | Pros | Cons | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| **(A) Download at install time** | Small ZIP (~no core overhead). Always latest WP. | Requires outbound HTTPS to `wordpress.org` and `raw.githubusercontent.com` for `wp-cli.phar`. Fails on locked-down hosts. | Default. Try first. |
| **(B) Bundled core** | Works offline. Reproducible — install matches the version that exported. | ZIP is +30-50MB. Bundle's WP version may be older than current at install time. | Fallback when (A) fails (no outbound) or when the export user opts in. |

Implementation:

- Export-time toggle: "Include WordPress core for offline self-boot" (default off; on doubles ZIP size).
- Installer probes outbound connectivity by HEAD-requesting `https://wordpress.org/`. If reachable → (A). If not, look for `wordpress/` folder in the ZIP root (= bundled core path). If neither → render an error explaining the operator needs to extract WordPress core into `wordpress/` manually before re-running.
- WP-CLI: bundle `wp-cli.phar` always (it's only ~6MB). Skips the connectivity round-trip for the most fragile step.

## Files to modify

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `inc/site-exporter/class-self-boot-builder.php` (NEW) | Generates `index.php` and `readme.txt` text. Pure string assembly + token substitution from a template. Templates live under `views/site-exporter/self-boot/`. |
| `views/site-exporter/self-boot/index.php.tpl` (NEW) | The self-boot installer template. Single-file PHP — no autoloader, no namespaces, no Composer. Must run on PHP 7.4+. |
| `views/site-exporter/self-boot/readme.txt` (NEW) | Human-readable extraction + import guide template. |
| `inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php` | In `handle_site_export()` (line 2032) and the new `handle_network_export()` from #1149: after the bundle is built, call `Self_Boot_Builder::add_to_bundle($staging_dir, $bundle_type, $manifest)`. New export-form toggle: "Make ZIP self-booting" (default **on**). |
| `inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php` (export-form modal) | Add toggle `include_self_boot` to `render_export_site_modal()` (line 1334) and to the network export form from #1149. |
| `tests/WP_Ultimo/Site_Exporter/Self_Boot_Builder_Test.php` (NEW) | Tests as listed under Verification. |

## Reference patterns to copy

- **Adding files to a bundle pre-zip:** existing pattern in `inc/site-exporter/mu-migration/includes/commands/class-mu-migration-export.php:506-528` (`$files_to_zip` array). Self-boot files go alongside.
- **Template rendering:** the codebase uses plain PHP templates under `views/`. Single-file installer matches the style of `views/sso/`, etc. — no Twig, no Blade.
- **Authenticated download/redirect:** `inc/site-exporter/class-export-download-handler.php` for the post-install redirect-to-wp-admin pattern.
- **Plugin self-installation:** look at how `inc/installers/` modules use `WP_Upgrader` for plugin installation — the self-boot installer can call into core's `Plugin_Upgrader` once WP is bootstrapped.

## Implementation notes / gotchas

1. **The installer runs without WordPress.** `index.php` cannot use any `wp_*` / `__()` / WordPress functions for the wizard UI. Plain PHP only. After WP is installed (step 5), it CAN bootstrap WordPress (`require_once 'wordpress/wp-load.php'`) and use WP functions for the import step.
2. **CSRF for the wizard.** Generate a one-time token on first GET, write it to a temp file (`.wu-bootstrap-token` with 0600 perms), require it on POST. Delete on success. Do not rely on PHP sessions (target may not have `session_save_path` writable).
3. **PHP-side validation.** `proc_open` / `exec` may be disabled on shared hosts. The installer must work without them — invoke WP-CLI via `include 'wp-cli.phar'` if available (WP-CLI's phar can be `require`'d for some commands), or fall back to manual PHP equivalents (raw mysqli for the SQL load, native `wp_install()` after `wp-load.php`).
4. **Detect existing install correctly.** `wp-config.php` presence is necessary but not sufficient — operator may have started but aborted an install. Also check for `siteurl` row in `wp_options`. If install partial, offer to resume.
5. **Idempotency.** Re-hitting `index.php` after a partial failure must not re-attempt completed steps. Track step state in `.wu-bootstrap-state.json` next to the installer. Steps: `db_credentials`, `core_acquired`, `core_installed`, `plugin_installed`, `bundle_imported`, `complete`.
6. **Self-deletion safety.** On success, delete `index.php` and `readme.txt`, but keep the audit log and the source ZIP (operator may want to re-run). Never auto-delete the bundle.
7. **HTTPS at self-boot time.** Target may not have HTTPS configured yet — installer must work over HTTP. Document this in `readme.txt`. Importing into HTTPS-target-from-HTTP-export should rewrite URLs accordingly via the existing `new_url` mechanism.
8. **Plugin install source.** Three options: (a) bundle the plugin source in the ZIP under `wp-ultimate-plugin/`, (b) download from `wordpress.org/plugins/` at install time, (c) download from a configurable GitHub release URL. Recommend **(a) bundle by default**, fallback **(b)** if not bundled. Reasoning: the export was made WITH a specific plugin version active; the import should use the same version, not a possibly-incompatible newer release. Bundling adds ~3-5MB.
9. **Multi-step wizard UX.** Five steps minimum: (1) DB credentials, (2) site URL + admin, (3) acquiring core (progress), (4) running import (progress + per-site status for network bundles), (5) done. Progress page should auto-refresh via meta refresh — the installer cannot rely on JS being available on every host.
10. **Capability to run export with `include_self_boot`:** `manage_network`. The toggle should be visible to anyone who can already export.
11. **PHP version detection.** `index.php` checks `PHP_VERSION` against `network.json.source.php_version`. If target's PHP is **lower** than source's, refuse with a clear error (forward-compat is best-effort, backward-compat is not). If target is higher, proceed with a warning.
12. **`readme.txt` format.** Plain text, ~80 column wrap, follows WordPress plugin readme convention so it's familiar. Must include: extraction instructions, manual import via WP-CLI alternative, troubleshooting (common errors: DB perms, file perms, outbound blocked), where to get help.

## Verification

- [ ] `npm run check` passes.
- [ ] Tests:
  - [ ] `test_self_boot_builder_adds_index_and_readme_to_staging_dir()`.
  - [ ] `test_self_boot_index_template_is_php_74_compatible()` — `php -l` on the rendered output.
  - [ ] `test_self_boot_index_refuses_on_existing_install()`.
  - [ ] `test_self_boot_token_csrf()` — POST without token rejected.
  - [ ] `test_self_boot_resume_after_partial_failure()` — corrupt the state file mid-flow, re-run, verify resume from last good step.
- [ ] Manual end-to-end (single-site bundle):
  - Export site with `include_self_boot: true`.
  - Extract ZIP onto a fresh `wordpress2.local:8080` webroot (no WP installed, no plugin).
  - Hit the URL, complete wizard with valid DB creds.
  - Verify: site loads at the new URL, admin login works, plugin is network-active (or single-active depending on bundle), `index.php` and `readme.txt` are gone, `wu-bootstrap-complete.log` exists.
- [ ] Manual end-to-end (network bundle, after #1149 + #1150):
  - Same as above but with a 3-site network bundle.
  - Verify: multisite is created, all 3 sites accessible at the operator's chosen domain pattern, designated main site is `blog_id = 1`.
- [ ] Manual offline test:
  - Export with bundled core option ON.
  - Block outbound on the target (drop rules to `wordpress.org`).
  - Verify wizard completes using bundled `wordpress/` folder.
- [ ] Manual hostile-environment test:
  - Disable `proc_open`/`exec` in `php.ini` on target.
  - Verify installer falls back to PHP-native paths and still completes.

## Open questions for the implementer (decide in PR description)

1. **Bundled core toggle default:** off (smaller ZIPs, requires connectivity) or on (always works, doubles size)? I lean **off by default with a prominent warning** in the export form ("Target server must have outbound internet to wordpress.org").
2. **Plugin source for self-install:** bundle / wordpress.org / GitHub release URL? I lean **bundle**.
3. **Wizard styling:** plain HTML (universal compatibility) or a small bundled CSS file (looks better, slightly more risk on weird hosts)? Lean **plain HTML with inline CSS** — no external requests.
4. **Should the installer support running over CLI?** `php index.php --db-host=... --db-user=... ...` for headless/server-imaging use? Nice-to-have, can be a follow-up.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by #1149** (network export — bundle format determines what the installer must restore).
- **Compatible with Issue B** (network import — `index.php` will call `wu_exporter_import_network()` if available, fall back to per-site loop otherwise).

title: fix(cloudways): exclude wildcards from Let's Encrypt SSL request, keep them in aliases
body:
## Summary

`Cloudways_Domain_Mapping::get_valid_ssl_domains()` currently includes wildcard
entries from `WU_CLOUDWAYS_EXTRA_DOMAINS` in the Let's Encrypt SSL request — it
strips the leading `*.` and passes the apex to Cloudways' `/security/lets_encrypt_install`
endpoint. Combined with `Cloudways_Integration::send_cloudways_request()`
hard-coding `'wild_card' => false`, this can collide with manually-installed
wildcard certificates and prevent per-tenant custom domains from getting SSL
(see #1141 for the user report).

The integration should **drop wildcard entries from the SSL request entirely**
while still keeping them on the **aliases** list (Cloudways needs them in
aliases for routing, but they have no place in a non-wildcard Let's Encrypt
request).

## Why

- Wildcards in the SSL list are guaranteed to be wrong: the integration always
  sends `wild_card => false`, so requesting Let's Encrypt for an apex stripped
  from a wildcard either silently accepts a non-wildcard apex cert (not what
  the user expects) or noisily fails DNS validation when the apex doesn't
  resolve to the network IP (most multisite setups).
- Aliases must still contain the wildcard so subsite routing on Cloudways works.
- The doc PRs (#1159, Ultimate-Multisite/docs#45) tell users not to put their
  network's wildcard in `WU_CLOUDWAYS_EXTRA_DOMAINS`, but that constant is
  legitimately useful for **external** wildcards (e.g. a wildcard on a separate
  marketing domain shared with the same Cloudways app). The code should handle
  any wildcard correctly — keep it in aliases, exclude it from the SSL request.

## Files to Modify

- `EDIT: inc/integrations/providers/cloudways/class-cloudways-domain-mapping.php:197-220`
  — change `get_valid_ssl_domains()` to **filter out** wildcard entries instead
  of stripping the `*.` prefix. The aliases path
  (`get_domains()` / `sync_domains()`) must keep wildcards untouched.
- `EDIT: tests/WP_Ultimo/Integrations/Providers/Cloudways_Domain_Mapping_Test.php`
  — add regression tests covering: (a) wildcard in `WU_CLOUDWAYS_EXTRA_DOMAINS`
  is present in the aliases payload, (b) the same wildcard is **absent** from
  the `ssl_domains` payload, (c) plain (non-wildcard) extra domains still flow
  to both. Use the existing `getMockBuilder(Cloudways_Integration::class)`
  pattern from the test file (line 16-18).

## How (Approach)

### Current implementation (the defect)

```php
// inc/integrations/providers/cloudways/class-cloudways-domain-mapping.php:197-220
private function get_valid_ssl_domains(array $domains): array {

    $ssl_domains = array_unique(
        array_map(
            function ($domain) {
                if (str_starts_with($domain, '*.')) {
                    $domain = str_replace('*.', '', $domain); // ← strips, retains apex
                }
                return $domain;
            },
            $domains
        )
    );

    $ssl_valid_domains = $this->check_domain_dns($ssl_domains, Helper::get_network_public_ip());
    // ...
}
```

### Proposed fix

Filter wildcards out before DNS validation rather than stripping. Apex of a
wildcard (`reddomain.com` from `*.reddomain.com`) is **not** the same domain
the user intended to certify, and we have no signal that DNS for the apex
resolves to the Cloudways IP.

```php
private function get_valid_ssl_domains(array $domains): array {

    // Drop wildcard entries entirely — Cloudways' Let's Encrypt endpoint here
    // never issues wildcard certs (wild_card => false), so wildcards in the
    // SSL list are meaningless. They must still appear on the aliases list,
    // which is unaffected by this method.
    $ssl_domains = array_values(
        array_filter(
            $domains,
            static fn ($domain) => ! str_starts_with((string) $domain, '*.')
        )
    );

    $ssl_valid_domains = $this->check_domain_dns($ssl_domains, Helper::get_network_public_ip());

    $main_domain = get_current_site()->domain;

    $ssl_valid_domains[] = $main_domain;

    return array_values(array_unique(array_filter($ssl_valid_domains)));
}
```

`get_domains()` (used for the aliases call) is unchanged — wildcards continue to
flow into `sync_domains()` → `/app/manage/aliases` as before.

### Verification

```bash
# Lint and stan the changed file:
vendor/bin/phpcs inc/integrations/providers/cloudways/class-cloudways-domain-mapping.php
vendor/bin/phpstan analyse inc/integrations/providers/cloudways/class-cloudways-domain-mapping.php

# Run the cloudways test class:
vendor/bin/phpunit --filter Cloudways_Domain_Mapping_Test
```

The new tests should assert the SSL payload (captured via the existing
`send_cloudways_request` mock) contains the right shape for both
`/app/manage/aliases` and `/security/lets_encrypt_install` calls when
`WU_CLOUDWAYS_EXTRA_DOMAINS` includes a wildcard like `*.example.com`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `get_valid_ssl_domains()` no longer emits the apex of any `*.x` entry into the SSL request.
- [ ] Wildcards remain in the aliases payload (`/app/manage/aliases`) — `sync_domains()` behaviour unchanged.
- [ ] New PHPUnit cases in `Cloudways_Domain_Mapping_Test` cover the aliases-yes / SSL-no split for a wildcard extra-domain.
- [ ] `vendor/bin/phpcs` clean on the modified file.
- [ ] `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse` clean on the modified file.
- [ ] `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter Cloudways_Domain_Mapping_Test` green.

## Context

- User report: #1141

title: fix(domain-mapping): wp_send_json in verify_dns_mapping triggers malformed get_option(blog_charset) query during early multisite bootstrap
body:
## Bug

Sites running Ultimate Multisite emit a WordPress database error on every request that triggers the async DNS-check path inside `WP_Ultimo\Domain_Mapping::verify_dns_mapping()`:

```
WordPress database error You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that
corresponds to your MariaDB server version for the right syntax to use near
'WHERE option_name = 'blog_charset' LIMIT 1' at line 1 for query
SELECT option_value FROM  WHERE option_name = 'blog_charset' LIMIT 1 made by
require('wp-blog-header.php'), require_once('wp-load.php'), require_once('wp-config.php'),
require_once('wp-settings.php'), require('wp-includes/ms-settings.php'),
ms_load_current_site_and_network, get_site_by_path, apply_filters('pre_get_site_by_path'),
WP_Hook->apply_filters, WP_Ultimo\Domain_Mapping->check_domain_mapping,
WP_Ultimo\Domain_Mapping->verify_dns_mapping, wp_send_json, get_option
```

Note the malformed query: `SELECT option_value FROM  WHERE …` — the table name between `FROM` and `WHERE` is empty.

## Root cause

`verify_dns_mapping()` is hooked on `pre_get_site_by_path` and `ms_site_not_found`, both of which fire from inside `ms_load_current_site_and_network()` at `wp-includes/ms-settings.php:77`.

The WP core bootstrap order is:

1. `wp-includes/ms-settings.php:46` — `require ms-load.php`.
2. `wp-includes/ms-settings.php:77` — `ms_load_current_site_and_network( … )` runs **and fires `pre_get_site_by_path` here**.
3. `wp-includes/ms-settings.php:102-103` — `$wpdb->set_prefix( $table_prefix, false )` and `$wpdb->set_blog_id( … )` run.

Until step 3, `$wpdb->options` is the empty string. When the async DNS-check path inside `verify_dns_mapping()` calls `wp_send_json($mapping->to_array())` (`inc/class-domain-mapping.php:375`), `wp_send_json()` calls `get_option( 'blog_charset' )` (`wp-includes/functions.php:4556`) before sending the `Content-Type` header. That `get_option()` queries `SELECT option_value FROM {$wpdb->options} …` — with `$wpdb->options` empty — which is what produces the malformed SQL and the noisy error.

The other DB call in the same path, `Domain::get_by_domain()` (`inc/models/class-domain.php:704-706`), already handles this early-bootstrap case by deriving the mapped-domains table name from `$wpdb->base_prefix` (which is set from `wp-config.php` before sunrise). `wp_send_json()` does not.

## Reproduction

1. WordPress Multisite with Ultimate Multisite active and at least one mapped domain.
2. Any request that fires the `async_check_dns_nonce` path (e.g. the loopback DNS-verification request triggered by the Domain Mapping screen).
3. The error appears in PHP/MariaDB logs on every such request.

## Proposed fix

In `verify_dns_mapping()`, replace the call to `wp_send_json()` with a bootstrap-safe direct emit:

- Send `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` directly with `header()` (UTF-8 is the WordPress default for `blog_charset`).
- `echo wp_json_encode( $payload )` (defined in `wp-includes/functions.php`, loaded earlier in `wp-settings.php:117`, well before `ms-settings.php`).
- `exit;`.

Extract the emit step into a small protected method (`send_async_dns_response()`) and add a `wu_async_dns_response_short_circuit` filter so plugins and tests can intercept the response without invoking `exit`.

## Files to modify

- `inc/class-domain-mapping.php` — `verify_dns_mapping()` (line ~363) and new `send_async_dns_response()`.
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Domain_Mapping_Test.php` — add a regression test that simulates the empty-`$wpdb->options` state and asserts the call produces no `wpdb->last_error`.

## Reference patterns

- `Domain::get_by_domain()` (`inc/models/class-domain.php:704`) — established pattern for handling early-bootstrap DB references with `$wpdb->base_prefix` fallback.
- WordPress core `wp_send_json()` (`wp-includes/functions.php:4541`) — shows the dependency on `get_option('blog_charset')` we need to avoid.

## Verification

```bash
composer install
vendor/bin/phpcs inc/class-domain-mapping.php
vendor/bin/phpstan analyse inc/class-domain-mapping.php
vendor/bin/phpunit --filter Domain_Mapping_Test
```

The added regression test fails on `main` (would emit the malformed `SELECT option_value FROM  WHERE …` query into `$wpdb->last_error`) and passes after the fix.

title: [URGENT] Password reset emails on subsites point to main site (broken UX for end customers)
body:
## TL;DR

When a user requests a password reset on **any subsite** (whether on a `*.networksite.com` subdomain or a **mapped custom domain**), the reset link in the email points to the **main network site's `wp-login.php`** instead of the subsite the user actually signed up on.

For networks like ours (a SaaS where each customer runs their **own brand on their own mapped domain**), this is a serious problem. **The end customers of our customers can't reset their passwords without leaving the brand they trust.**

## Real-world impact (production)

We run a multisite SaaS on UM 2.10.1 where each customer is a subsite with their own mapped custom domain. Real bug report received today:

- User `zuletadia` registered on subsite `yariglam.cl` (mapped custom domain).
- She requests a password reset from `yariglam.cl/mi-cuenta/lost-password/`.
- She receives an email with this link:
  ```
  https://kursopro.com/wp-login.php?action=rp&key=...&login=zuletadia
  ```
- She is taken to **kursopro.com** (the network owner's domain), a brand she doesn't recognize, and asked to set her password there.
- She thinks it's phishing or doesn't trust it. **Customer of our customer is lost.**

This affects every subsite in the network, not just mapped domains.

## Cause

In `inc/checkout/class-checkout-pages.php`, function `replace_reset_password_link()` (line 354) returns early on subsites:

```php
public function replace_reset_password_link($message, $key, $user_login, $user_data) {
    if ( ! is_main_site()) {
        return $message;  // ← subsite: nothing rewritten, default URL points to main site wp-login.php
    }
    ...
}
```

Combined with the fact that the `add_filter('retrieve_password_message', ...)` registration is itself wrapped inside `if (is_main_site())` (line 67), the filter never even runs on subsites.

The result: WordPress's default `retrieve_password()` builds the URL with `network_site_url('wp-login.php')`, which on every subsite resolves to **the main site's wp-login**. UM has no chance to fix it.

## Reproduction (verified on 8 subsites in staging)

```
[BLOG 302 yariglam.cl]                       URL host = kpstage.com  ← FAIL (mapped .cl domain)
[BLOG 303 ekgcommunity.kpstage.com]          URL host = kpstage.com  ← FAIL
[BLOG 305 cursosdemaquillaje...kpstage.com]  URL host = kpstage.com  ← FAIL
[BLOG 306 blickclub.kpstage.com]             URL host = kpstage.com  ← FAIL
[BLOG 308 cora.kpstage.com]                  URL host = kpstage.com  ← FAIL
[BLOG 310 enpasapalosacademy.kpstage.com]    URL host = kpstage.com  ← FAIL
[BLOG 311 luna.kpstage.com]                  URL host = kpstage.com  ← FAIL
[BLOG 313 coloritos.kpstage.com]             URL host = kpstage.com  ← FAIL
```

8/8 subsites broken on UM 2.10.1 with `enable_custom_login_page=1`, `default_login_page=1516`.

## Proposed fix

PR #XXXX (link below) makes `replace_reset_password_link()` subsite-aware:

- On main site: behaviour unchanged (URL → custom login page).
- On a subsite: the URL is rewritten to `home_url('/')` of that subsite with the original `action=rp / key / login / wp_lang` query args, so existing handlers (WooCommerce my-account, BuddyPress, custom themes, wp-login fallback) can complete the reset on the subsite's own domain.
- The hook registration is moved out of the `is_main_site()` branch so it actually runs on subsites.
- New filter `wu_subsite_password_reset_url` lets integrations point at a specific endpoint (e.g. WooCommerce `lost-password`).

## Tested on staging

Patch validated on 8 subsites including a real `.cl` mapped domain. **8/8 PASS** in unit-level filter test, **7/8 PASS** end-to-end via real `retrieve_password()` flow (1 unrelated SMTP rate-limit). Main site regression check: OK.

## Why urgent

This is happening to live customers right now. Every subsite owner whose end customers try to reset a password loses brand trust. Please prioritize.

Will open the PR linked to this issue.

title: Enhance integration: domain deletion broken due to `id`/`domainId` field mismatch in lookup
body:
## Summary

The Enhance integration adds domains successfully, but **never deletes them**. Every removal attempt logs `Could not find domain ID for X, it may have already been removed` even when the domain is clearly present in the GET response. As a result, deleted sites in Ultimate Multisite leave orphan domain entries on Enhance forever.

This is reproducible on the latest released version of the plugin.

## Root cause (confirmed in source)

The Enhance API returns the domain UUID under **two different field names** depending on the endpoint:

| Endpoint | Field name | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /orgs/{org}/websites/{site}/domains` | `id` | `{"id":"33f39bbf-..."}` |
| `GET /orgs/{org}/websites/{site}/domains` | `domainId` | `{"items":[{"domain":"...", "domainId":"b40e582a-...", ...}]}` |

The deletion lookup reads `$item['id']` from the GET-list response, where the field is actually called `domainId`. The match never assigns a UUID, `$domain_id` stays `null`, and DELETE is never sent.

**File:** `inc/integrations/providers/enhance/class-enhance-domain-mapping.php`, line 177:

```php
foreach ($domains_list['items'] as $item) {
    if (isset($item['domain']) && $item['domain'] === $domain) {
        $domain_id = $item['id']; // ← reads 'id'; GET response uses 'domainId'
        break;
    }
}

if (empty($domain_id)) {
    wu_log_add('integration-enhance', sprintf('Could not find domain ID for %s, it may have already been removed', $domain));
    return;
}
```

The addition path (a few lines up) reads `id` from the POST response, which is correct — the asymmetry is on Enhance's side, not in the plugin elsewhere.

## Reproduction

1. Configure the Enhance integration with valid credentials.
2. Create a new subsite in Ultimate Multisite. → Enhance receives the domain (POST returns 201 with `{"id": "..."}`).
3. Delete the subsite permanently from Ultimate Multisite. → Integration logs the lookup attempt and gives up.
4. Check Enhance: the alias domain is still there.

Happens 100% of the time across many test sites in my logs.

## Log evidence

Add (`musteri1.asfsv5.com`):

```
[2026-05-09 12:26:02] Adding domain: musteri1.asfsv5.com for site ID: 2
[2026-05-09 12:26:02] Making POST request to: https://asf.asfsv4.com/api/orgs/<org>/websites/<site>/domains
[2026-05-09 12:26:02] Request data: {"domain":"musteri1.asfsv5.com"}
[2026-05-09 12:26:02] API response code: 201, body: {"id":"b40e582a-367f-48ab-8f05-0431b0212f4b"}
[2026-05-09 12:26:02] Domain musteri1.asfsv5.com added successfully.
```

Delete attempt (same domain):

```
[2026-05-09 13:01:24] Removing domain: musteri1.asfsv5.com for site ID: 2
[2026-05-09 13:01:24] Making GET request to: https://asf.asfsv4.com/api/orgs/<org>/websites/<site>/domains
[2026-05-09 13:01:24] API response code: 200, body: {"items":[
  {"domain":"musteri1.asfsv5.com","domainId":"b40e582a-367f-48ab-8f05-0431b0212f4b","websiteId":"...","mappingKind":"alias",...},
  ...
]}
[2026-05-09 13:01:24] Could not find domain ID for musteri1.asfsv5.com, it may have already been removed
```

The UUID `b40e582a-367f-48ab-8f05-0431b0212f4b` is right there in the response under `domainId`. **No DELETE request is ever sent.**

## API verification (manual test)

To rule out an API-side issue, I sent two manual DELETE requests directly from the Enhance panel session (Chrome DevTools console, `fetch()` with `credentials: 'include'`):

1. **Org-level endpoint** (the one Enhance's own UI uses for domain deletion):
   `DELETE /api/orgs/{org}/domains/{domainId}` → **204 No Content**, domain removed.

2. **Website-level endpoint** (the one this plugin's URL pattern targets):
   `DELETE /api/orgs/{org}/websites/{site}/domains/{domainId}` → **204 No Content**, domain removed.

Both endpoints work and accept the UUID returned under `domainId` in the GET list. The plugin's URL pattern is fine; only the lookup is broken.

## Suggested fix

Single-line change at the lookup, accepting both field names so the plugin is resilient if Enhance harmonizes them later:

```php
$domain_id = $item['domainId'] ?? $item['id'] ?? null;
```

The POST-response check and addition path stay as-is.

## Additional observation (probably a separate issue)

Every add and remove call fires **twice** back-to-back in the same second. Adds are idempotent on Enhance (second call gets `409 already_exists`), so no data corruption — but worth investigating. The same double-firing happens on remove (two consecutive `Removing domain: ...` log lines for the same site delete). Happy to file this as a separate issue if useful.

## Environment

- Ultimate Multisite: 2.10.1 (latest release at time of writing)
- WordPress: <6.9.4>
- PHP: 8.4 (
- Enhance: cloud-hosted control panel

I have the full integration-enhance log file available; happy to attach if helpful.

title: bug: `wp search-replace` fatals for every developer due to vendored wp-cli/search-replace-command incompatible with WP-CLI 2.12 phar
body:
## Summary

`wp search-replace` fatals when run from any contributor's checkout of this plugin against a WordPress install where the plugin is active. The vendored `wp-cli/search-replace-command` v2.1.11 pulled in by `wp-cli/wp-cli-bundle` (require-dev) is incompatible with the WP-CLI 2.12.0 phar's internal `SearchReplacer`. This blocks every developer who needs to run `wp search-replace` while developing the plugin (URL changes, prefix migrations, dev-data scrubbing, etc.).

## Reproduction

1. `composer install` on this repo (installs `wp-cli/wp-cli-bundle ^2.12` → vendors `wp-cli/search-replace-command v2.1.11` into `vendor/`).
2. Activate the plugin in a WordPress install (the dev install at `../wordpress`).
3. Run any `wp search-replace ...` command from the repo root with global WP-CLI 2.12.0 phar (`/usr/local/bin/wp`):

   ```bash
   wp search-replace 'foo' 'bar' --dry-run
   ```

4. Fatal:

   ```
   Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to undefined method Search_Replace_Command::json_encode_strip_quotes()
     in /home/.../ultimate-multisite/vendor/wp-cli/search-replace-command/src/WP_CLI/SearchReplacer.php:92
   Stack trace:
   #0 phar:///usr/local/bin/wp/vendor/wp-cli/search-replace-command/src/Search_Replace_Command.php(539):
        WP_CLI\SearchReplacer->__construct()
   ...
   ```

The same fatal occurs even when running `wp` from outside the repo (e.g. `/tmp`), as long as the plugin is active in the target WordPress — because the plugin's `vendor/autoload.php` is loaded by WordPress and registers the older classes before the phar's classes are looked up.

## Root Cause

- `composer.json` `require-dev` declares `"wp-cli/wp-cli-bundle": "^2.12"`.
- The bundle transitively installs `wp-cli/search-replace-command v2.1.11` under `vendor/wp-cli/search-replace-command/` (per `composer.lock`).
- The class names `Search_Replace_Command` and `WP_CLI\SearchReplacer` are global (not namespaced) and are also shipped inside the WP-CLI phar at `phar:///usr/local/bin/wp/vendor/wp-cli/search-replace-command/`.
- When the plugin is active, `vendor/autoload.php` runs early and registers the older v2.1.11 `Search_Replace_Command` (which does not have `json_encode_strip_quotes()`).
- The newer phar-bundled `SearchReplacer` (v2.13+ inside WP-CLI 2.12.0) calls `Search_Replace_Command::json_encode_strip_quotes($from)` and fatals because that method only exists in the newer class.

The two versions are wire-incompatible: phar bumped `Search_Replace_Command::json_encode_strip_quotes()` from `protected` to `public static` (or added the method outright) in a release after v2.1.11, but the phar's `SearchReplacer` was updated to require it.

## Why It Affects Everyone

Any developer who:
1. Runs `composer install` (every contributor — required to set up the repo).
2. Has the plugin active in the WordPress dev install at `../wordpress` (the documented setup in `AGENTS.md`).
3. Uses the standard global WP-CLI phar (the documented `wp` command in `AGENTS.md`).

…will hit this fatal on every `wp search-replace` invocation.

## Impact

- Cannot reset/scrub dev data with `wp search-replace` URL/prefix migrations.
- `bin/install-wp-tests.sh` workflows that use search-replace fail.
- Site export/import dev workflows that rely on search-replace fail.

## Proposed Fixes (one of)

1. **Pin the vendored package to a version compatible with WP-CLI 2.12** — bump the install constraint so composer pulls `wp-cli/search-replace-command ^2.2` (which has the same `json_encode_strip_quotes` signature as the phar). Verify by running:

   ```bash
   composer update wp-cli/search-replace-command
   wp search-replace 'a' 'b' --dry-run
   ```

2. **Drop `wp-cli/wp-cli-bundle` from `require-dev` entirely** — the bundle isn't needed for unit tests; phpunit runs standalone. The dev install uses the global WP-CLI phar, not the vendored bundle. This is the cleanest fix.

3. **Add a composer `conflict` or `replace` entry** for `wp-cli/search-replace-command` so the vendored copy is never autoloaded when the phar's copy is present. (Complex; option 2 is simpler.)

Option 2 (`require-dev` cleanup) is recommended — `wp-cli/wp-cli-bundle` was probably added for one-off `wp` invocations during testing but its presence breaks the standard `wp` command for everyone.

- `composer.json` — remove `"wp-cli/wp-cli-bundle": "^2.12"` from `require-dev` (line ~81).
- `composer.lock` — regenerate via `composer update --no-install` then `composer install`.

After the fix:

```bash
composer install
wp plugin activate ultimate-multisite
wp search-replace 'test-old-string-xyz' 'test-new-string-xyz' --dry-run
# Should succeed with a "0 replacements" report, not fatal.
```

title: Inventory of mu-plugin patches we run on a 300-subsite production multisite (kursopro.com) — open offer to upstream any of these
body:
Hi David,

This is **not a bug report** — it's an inventory. We run a multisite SaaS on top of Ultimate Multisite (kursopro.com, ~300 subsites, ~50 mapped custom domains) and over the past six months we accumulated a set of mu-plugins that patch behaviour we couldn't fix upstream quickly enough during production incidents.

Some of these are real bugs in UM core. Some are backports of code we found in your `main` branch but that hadn't been released. Some are workarounds for races that surface only at production scale.

We are not opening 8 PRs at once. We don't want to flood your queue. **What we'd like to do is give you complete visibility into what we're patching**, and then prepare a clean PR for any item you'd like to absorb upstream. You pick the order. You pick which ones are even in scope for UM core. If a workaround is too KursoPro-specific to upstream, just say so and we'll keep it on our side.

## Where to read the actual code

All eight mu-plugins are in a read-only reference branch on our fork:

**https://github.com/kenedytorcatt/ultimate-multisite/tree/reference/kursopro-mu-plugins-inventory/.kursopro-reference**

The README in that folder cross-references each file.

## What each one does

### 1. `kp-um-template-switch-fix.php` (v3.5.0, ~1800 LOC)

[Source](https://github.com/kenedytorcatt/ultimate-multisite/blob/reference/kursopro-mu-plugins-inventory/.kursopro-reference/mu-plugins/kp-um-template-switch-fix.php)

Patches the `wu_switch_template` AJAX handler. 10 bugs grouped into one file:

1. AJAX timeout (default 30s) cuts `copy_files` mid-process on large templates.
2. `blogname` overwritten with the source template's title.
3. `blogmeta` corruption when AJAX dies mid-flight.
4. Elementor Kit / CSS broken post-switch (incomplete regen — only 30 posts).
5. Object cache returns stale `wu_type` after restore.
6. No recovery path for affected customers — required manual SQL.
7. Elementor fatal `get_responsive_control_duplication_mode() on null` because `Plugin::$instance->breakpoints` is not initialised when `MUCD_Data::copy_data()` runs.
8. No "reset current template" option in the UI — user has to switch to a different template and back.
9. Thumbnail (panel preview) not refreshed when template changes.
10. **Kit Elementor settings/data NOT copied during `MUCD_Data::copy_data()`.** Real case 2026-05-03: customer `abconline` switched to template "Belleza" but Kit retained colours from previous "Profesional" (blue `#305778` instead of pink `#EAC7C7`). Root cause: MUCD copies `wp_X_postmeta` rows but the Elementor Kit (post 3) settings serialize/cache layer doesn't pick up the new values without explicit force-copy + regen.

The mu-plugin works entirely through public hooks. If you want this upstream, the natural home is:
- `inc/helpers/class-site-duplicator.php :: override_site()`
- `inc/ui/class-template-switching-element.php :: switch_template()`

Tell us and we'll prep a PR.

### 2. `kp-um-cookieless-sso.php` (v1.0.1)

[Source](https://github.com/kenedytorcatt/ultimate-multisite/blob/reference/kursopro-mu-plugins-inventory/.kursopro-reference/mu-plugins/kp-um-cookieless-sso.php)

**This is a backport of your own code.** The plugin header points at commits `7012d4a8`, `9b011840`, `70c2216d` on your `main` branch. We ported them onto 2.9.2 in May 2025 because Chrome's third-party cookie blocking was breaking iframe'd admin on mapped domains for our customers, and we couldn't wait for v2.9.3+.

Two halves:
- **Emitter** on `init` priority 1: when a logged-in user is on the main site and `redirect_to` points at a mapped domain, append an HMAC-signed, single-use, 5-minute-expiry `wu_sso_token` query arg.
- **Receiver** on `init` priority 4: on mapped domain, if `?wu_sso_token=` is present, validate HMAC + exp + audience + jti, then `wp_set_auth_cookie()` and redirect to clean URL.

We've been running this in production since May 2025 with zero incidents. If you'd like it merged into core for 2.12.x, we can prep the PR with the production-hardened version (the original commits had a few edge cases we found and patched).

### 3. `kp-um-sso-loop-breaker.php` (v3.0.0)

[Source](https://github.com/kenedytorcatt/ultimate-multisite/blob/reference/kursopro-mu-plugins-inventory/.kursopro-reference/mu-plugins/kp-um-sso-loop-breaker.php)

Patches an SSO redirect loop on mapped domains: customer visits `javieraacademy.com/wp-admin` → `kursopro.com/login/?sso=login&redirect_to=...` → back to mapped domain → infinite loop. Triggered most reliably when a non-super-admin client visits a mapped subsite admin via an iframe (we use a frontend admin plugin called WPFA).

Strategy: counter cookie on the main domain. Once it hits a threshold within a short window, the SSO redirect is short-circuited and the user sees the regular login form instead of looping.

Your `065-sso-redirect-loop.spec.js` exists — overlap is partial but they cover different triggers. Happy to extend yours if useful.

### 4. `kp-sso-mapped-fix.php` (v1.1.0)

[Source](https://github.com/kenedytorcatt/ultimate-multisite/blob/reference/kursopro-mu-plugins-inventory/.kursopro-reference/mu-plugins/kp-sso-mapped-fix.php)

Admin bar SSO on mapped domains after PR #366 regression. PR #366 changed JSONP to not attach via redirect (which fixed a loop). Side effect: the admin bar never appears on the frontend of a mapped domain on first visit. Plugin restores it via an explicit attach call on `wp_loaded`.

### 5. `kp-fix-um-blogname.php` (v1.0.0)

[Source](https://github.com/kenedytorcatt/ultimate-multisite/blob/reference/kursopro-mu-plugins-inventory/.kursopro-reference/mu-plugins/kp-fix-um-blogname.php)

`inc/helpers/class-site-duplicator.php` around lines 326-327: `$args->title` is empty when the duplication is triggered by a WooCommerce checkout flow, so the new subsite ends up with the template's `blogname` ("Plantilla Belleza", "Plantilla Profesional", etc) instead of the customer's chosen site name.

Plugin force-applies the customer's title from `wu_checkout` order meta after duplication completes.

Reproduces on every WooCommerce checkout with site duplication.

### 6. `kp-fix-um-domain-mapping.php` (v1.0.0)

[Source](https://github.com/kenedytorcatt/ultimate-multisite/blob/reference/kursopro-mu-plugins-inventory/.kursopro-reference/mu-plugins/kp-fix-um-domain-mapping.php)

Three small fixes bundled:
- Adds missing `option_home` filter so `get_home_url()` returns the mapped domain.
- Flushes rewrite rules on new subsite creation (otherwise permalinks 404 until manual flush).
- Enforces HTTPS scheme on mapped domains.

### 7. `kp-um-bugs-fixes.php` (v1.0.0)

[Source](https://github.com/kenedytorcatt/ultimate-multisite/blob/reference/kursopro-mu-plugins-inventory/.kursopro-reference/mu-plugins/kp-um-bugs-fixes.php)

A bag of small defensive fixes against UM 2.9.1 + UM-WC 2.0.10. Each fix is gated by a `define()` constant so it can be disabled individually. Header lists every bug it covers — happy to split into separate items if you want to tackle them one by one.

### 8. `kp-um-cookie-less-sso-token.php` (v1.0.0)

[Source](https://github.com/kenedytorcatt/ultimate-multisite/blob/reference/kursopro-mu-plugins-inventory/.kursopro-reference/mu-plugins/kp-um-cookie-less-sso-token.php)

Earlier iteration of the cookie-less SSO backport (#2 in this list superseded it). Included for completeness in case the diff between versions is informative.

## What's already in flight on our side

- PR #1169 (subsite password reset URL) — **merged in 2.10.2**, thanks!
- PR #1185 (SSO bootstrap race / `$current_blog->registered` empty) — **merged in 2.11.1**, thanks!
- PR #1198 (Cypress regression guards for both fixes above) — currently a draft. We authored it on Windows without Docker, so it's draft until your CI can validate it.
- ultimate-multisite-captcha #82 (2FA OTP captcha re-validation lockout) — **merged in 1.4.1**, thanks!

## How to take this forward

Pick whichever you want and we'll prep a clean PR for it against `main`:

- [ ] Template switch fix (item 1) — biggest, highest impact, has a customer-visible failure case
- [ ] Cookie-less SSO backport (item 2) — finishes work you started on `main`
- [ ] SSO loop breaker on mapped domains (item 3)
- [ ] Admin bar SSO on mapped domains (item 4)
- [ ] Site duplication blogname (item 5)
- [ ] Domain mapping smaller fixes (item 6)
- [ ] Defensive bag (item 7) — would be split into individual items per bug
- [ ] None of the above — keep them as KursoPro-side patches

Whatever you say. We're patient. The production network is stable on 2.11.1 and these mu-plugins, so there's no urgency on our side.

Thank you for shipping #1168/#1169 and #1185 so quickly, and for #82 in the captcha plugin. Those three fixes together unblocked real users on real custom domains.

— Kenedy ([kenedytorcatt](https://github.com/kenedytorcatt))

title: fix(stripe): membership upgrade/downgrade fails with 'unknown parameter: coupon' from Stripe
body:
## Summary

When an admin upgrades or downgrades a membership (via *Memberships → Edit → Add New Product* in the network admin), saving the membership fails with the Stripe API error:

> Received unknown parameter: `coupon`. Did you mean to use `discounts` instead?

The error is rendered inside the *Add New Product* modal.

## Root cause

`Base_Stripe_Gateway::process_membership_update()` already uses the modern `discounts` array when applying a pro-rata credit coupon (the deprecated top-level `coupon` parameter was removed by Stripe in newer API versions). However:

1. When no credit coupon needs to be applied **but** the subscription still has a pre-existing discount, the gateway issues a second API call to the deprecated `subscriptions->deleteDiscount()` endpoint. This is fragile (two round trips, non-atomic) and a legacy code path.
2. Legacy filters or third-party addons that hook into `wu_stripe_create_subscription_args` could still inject a top-level `coupon` key into the subscription-create payload. No defensive guard exists today, so any such re-introduction surfaces as the exact error message above.

## Affected paths

- `inc/gateways/class-base-stripe-gateway.php::process_membership_update()` — admin add-product / upgrade-downgrade flow.
- `inc/gateways/class-base-stripe-gateway.php::create_subscription()` — initial checkout subscription create with optional pro-rata coupon.

## Proposed fix

- Fold the existing-discount clearing into the same `subscriptions->update` call by passing `discounts: []` instead of `subscriptions->deleteDiscount()`. Atomic, no deprecated SDK method.
- Defensively `unset($sub_args['coupon'])` after `apply_filters('wu_stripe_create_subscription_args', ...)` so legacy filters cannot re-introduce the deprecated top-level parameter.
- Log the parameter keys sent to Stripe (not values) when the update throws, so future regressions are diagnosable.

## Verification

- Existing `Base_Stripe_Gateway_Test` (107 tests, 181 assertions) passes with the change.
- Full `Stripe` filter run (194 tests) passes with exit 0.
- `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse inc/gateways/class-base-stripe-gateway.php` reports 0 errors.
- `vendor/bin/phpcs inc/gateways/class-base-stripe-gateway.php` reports no new violations (2 pre-existing on lines 2943 and 3320 are unrelated to this diff).

title: Checkout: 30s silent wait after submit; double-clicks break Cap captcha tokens
body:
## Summary

When the `/get-your-free-demo-site/` checkout form is submitted, the page becomes
unresponsive for ~30 seconds with no spinner, progress text, or button state
change. The user has no signal that the click registered. Instinctive double-clicks
or re-submissions can break the Cap captcha token flow (single-use tokens),
causing the checkout to silently fail in a way that does not produce a clear
error.

## Reproduction

1. With DNS in `none` (Cloudflare passthrough) or `prod` mode, open
   `https://ultimateagentwp.ai/get-your-free-demo-site/` while logged out.
2. Fill the form with a fresh email and click "Get Free Demo".
3. Observe: the submit button does not enter a disabled/loading state, no
   spinner appears, and the page sits visually idle for ~25-35 seconds before
   the redirect to `?payment=<id>&status=done`.

DevTools Network shows the sequence:

- `wu_cap_challenge` (POST, ~200 ms)
- `wu_cap_redeem` (POST, sometimes 500 then 200 on retry, ~1-3 s)
- `wu_check_user_exists` (POST, ~200 ms)
- *(then a 20-30 s gap with no visible activity)*
- `wu_create_order` and the final redirect

Observed on production `davidclaude@…` signup on 2026-05-18; screenshots
captured at `04-after-checkout-click.png` and `05-after-second-click.png`
(local session artefacts).

## Impact

- Many users will click twice or close the tab during the 30 s silence.
- Single-use Cap tokens make retries fragile: a token redeemed on the first
  click is invalid on the second, so the second attempt can show no progress
  at all (observed in the second verification run during the same session).
- Even users who wait see a janky experience that erodes trust before they
  reach the dashboard for the first time.

## Files

- `inc/checkout/class-checkout.php` — `wu_create_order` AJAX path; ~30 s of
  server work likely concentrates here (site cloning + gateway dispatch +
  autologin token issuance).
- `assets/js/checkout.js` (registered via `inc/checkout/class-checkout.php:3206`
  as `wu-checkout`) — client submit handler; no visible loading indicator
  between submit and redirect.
- `inc/duplication/option.php` and `inc/site-templates/class-template-placeholders.php`
  — synchronous template clone is a strong candidate for the wall-clock
  dominator.

Investigation needed in: which step dominates the 30 s (clone vs. email vs.
provisioning). Logging on the existing `wu_checkout_done` action would
localise the bottleneck quickly.

## Suggested fix

Two independent, low-risk improvements:

1. **Client UX (mandatory):** Disable the submit button and render a spinner
   plus status copy ("Provisioning your site — this can take up to 60
   seconds.") between submit and redirect. This alone eliminates the
   double-click failure mode.
2. **Server perf (follow-up):** Move heavy work (site clone, plugin sync) to
   an async step. `wu_create_order` returns immediately with a job id; the
   thank-you page polls until provisioning completes. The existing
   `pending_site` cleanup pattern documented under
   `AGENTS.md → Recurring Product Context` is the right place to hook in.

The minimum-viable PR is just (1).

## Verification

- Submit a fresh demo signup with DevTools Network throttling off; confirm the
  spinner appears immediately and the submit button is disabled until the
  redirect fires.
- Confirm no `wu_cap_*` request fires twice from a single click sequence.
- Optional: add a `wu_checkout_started`/`wu_checkout_done` timing log entry
  to capture the wall-clock duration for monitoring.

title: Production loads unminified Vue dev build via wu-vue script handle
body:
## Summary

The `wu-vue` script handle is registered with the **unminified development
build** of Vue (`assets/js/lib/vue.js`) rather than the production build
(`assets/js/lib/vue.min.js`). Every page that pulls in `wu-vue` — including
the public checkout — ships the dev build to end users, which prints the
"You are running Vue in development mode" warning, ships a larger payload
(~370 kB vs ~96 kB), and pays the dev-build runtime cost (warnings,
assertions).

## Reproduction

1. Visit any page that enqueues `wu-vue` (the public checkout at
   `/get-your-free-demo-site/` is a good test) in production.
2. View source / DevTools Network and confirm `assets/js/lib/vue.js?ver=...`
   is loaded (not `vue.min.js`).
3. Open the DevTools console and observe the Vue dev-mode warning.

Both files ship in the repo, so the production minified build exists and is
ready to use:

```
git ls-files 'assets/js/lib/vue*.js'
assets/js/lib/vue.js
assets/js/lib/vue.min.js
```

## Impact

- ~270 kB of unnecessary JS on every checkout (and every other Vue-enqueueing
  page) for every visitor.
- Production console noise (Vue's dev-mode banner).
- Slower hydration / runtime due to dev-build assertions; not catastrophic but
  measurable.
- This is the public-facing first impression for every prospect hitting the
  checkout.

## Files

- `inc/admin-pages/class-setup-wizard-admin-page.php:974`
  ```php
  wp_register_script('wu-vue', wu_get_asset('lib/vue.js', 'js'), [], wu_get_version(), true);
  ```
- `inc/checkout/class-checkout.php:3206` — registers `wu-checkout` with
  `wu-vue` as a dependency, which propagates the dev build to the public
  checkout.

Other Vue-related libs (`vue-the-mask`, `vue-draggable`, `vue-apexcharts`,
`v-money`) appear to be registered the same way and should be audited in the
same pass.

## Suggested fix

In `wu_get_asset()` (or in each `wp_register_script` call for the lib bundles),
swap to the `.min.js` variant when `SCRIPT_DEBUG` is not defined or false:

```php
$vue_asset = ( defined( 'SCRIPT_DEBUG' ) && SCRIPT_DEBUG )
    ? 'lib/vue.js'
    : 'lib/vue.min.js';
wp_register_script( 'wu-vue', wu_get_asset( $vue_asset, 'js' ), [], wu_get_version(), true );
```

The cleanest variant is to teach `wu_get_asset()` itself to auto-promote any
`lib/*.js` path to `lib/*.min.js` when both exist and `SCRIPT_DEBUG` is off
(mirroring how `inc/captcha-providers/class-cap-captcha-provider.php` uses the
sister `get_asset()` helper).

## Verification

- After fix, hard-reload the public checkout. DevTools Network shows
  `lib/vue.min.js` and no `lib/vue.js`. Console shows no Vue dev-mode banner.
- Verify the same for `wp-admin` Setup Wizard and any other Vue-using page.
- Re-load with `define('SCRIPT_DEBUG', true)` in `wp-config.php` and confirm
  the unminified `lib/vue.js` is served — the dev-mode path must still work.

title: fix: checkout submit button stays disabled after provisioning failure (regression from #1222)
body:
## Summary

PR #1222 correctly disabled submit buttons during checkout provisioning but the re-enable path is incomplete. On validation errors and API failure callbacks that call `unblock()`, the submit buttons remain disabled, leaving users unable to retry without a page reload.

## Root Cause

`assets/js/checkout.js` around lines 1630–1661: `jQuery(this).find('button[type="submit"]').prop('disabled', true)` fires before `that.block(loadingMessage)`, but failure/unblock paths do not call `.prop('disabled', false)`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Begin checkout provisioning (triggers spinner + button disable via PR #1222)
2. Trigger a failure: use an invalid payment method, network timeout, or coupon validation error
3. Spinner dismisses (unblock) but submit button stays disabled — user cannot retry

## Expected

Every path that calls `that.block(...)` or `unblock()` re-enables submit buttons via `.prop('disabled', false)`.

## Files

- `assets/js/checkout.js` — around lines 1630–1661

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All `unblock()` call sites in the checkout form submit handler also re-enable submit buttons
- [ ] Verified: submitting with a bad card → spinner appears → error message → submit button re-enables
- [ ] No regression on successful provisioning path (button should stay disabled until redirect/completion)

Identified by CodeRabbit review on PR #1222.

## Summary

title: Site creation after free checkout silently falls back to Action Scheduler (loopback fast-path nonce failure)
body:
## Summary

`Membership::publish_pending_site_async()` has a loopback HTTP "fast path" to `admin-ajax.php?action=wu_publish_pending_site` that is supposed to start site creation immediately after checkout. On stacks where the calling request has just auto-logged-in the customer (typical free-checkout path), this loopback is silently rejected by `check_ajax_referer()` and the site is only created later by the Action Scheduler fallback (`wu_async_publish_pending_site`). On servers where the network main site's WP-cron ticks infrequently (e.g. once an hour), customers wait up to an hour for their site instead of seeing it immediately.

There is **no log entry** when this happens, so operators have no signal that the fast path is broken.

## Reproduction (production evidence)

- WP 7.0-RC2, Ultimate Multisite 2.5.x, Action Scheduler 3.9.3
- FrankenPHP (no `fastcgi_finish_request`), free `plan_id=8` checkout via the `free` gateway
- Membership 54 / customer 54 / user 1037 / blog 80 (`davidnewtest.sdaiagent.com`)

Timeline:

| GMT | Event |
|---|---|
| 16:53:52 | Membership 54 created (`wp_wu_memberships.date_created`) |
| 16:53:52 | Action 82464 `wu_async_publish_pending_site` enqueued with `scheduled_date_gmt = now` |
| 16:53:55 | `checkout_completed` event written |
| 17:00:03 | Blog 80 row created in `wp_blogs` (= when AS queue tick fired) |
| 17:00:36 | Action 82464 marked `complete` |

**~7-minute gap between checkout and site existence**, attributable entirely to waiting for the next AS queue tick. The loopback fast path never created the site.

Direct probe of the AJAX endpoint from the same host (no cookies):

```
$ curl -sS -o - -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' \
    'https://mygratis.site/wp/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=wu_publish_pending_site&membership_id=54'
0HTTP 400
```

`check_ajax_referer()` rejected the request and emitted `0` + `die()` — exactly what the loopback fast-path receives.

## Root cause

`inc/models/class-membership.php:2110-2150`:

```php
$rest_path = add_query_arg([
    'action'        => 'wu_publish_pending_site',
    '_ajax_nonce'   => wp_create_nonce('wu_publish_pending_site'),
    'membership_id' => $this->get_id(),
], admin_url('admin-ajax.php'));

$request_args = [
    'cookies'   => wp_unslash($_COOKIE), // Cookies are needed for nonce check to work.
    'timeout'   => 10,
    'sslverify' => apply_filters('https_local_ssl_verify', false),
    'headers'   => $headers,
];

if ( ! function_exists('fastcgi_finish_request')) {
    $request_args['blocking'] = false;
}
$result = wp_remote_request($rest_path, $request_args);

if (is_wp_error($result)) {
    wu_log_add("membership-{$this->get_id()}", sprintf( /* … */ ));
}

wu_enqueue_async_action('wu_async_publish_pending_site', /* … */);
```

Three compounding defects:

1. **Stale cookies for new sessions.** `$_COOKIE` holds the cookies present in the *inbound* checkout request, before the customer was auto-logged-in. The calling PHP process now has a logged-in user (`wp_get_current_user()` returns the new customer), so `wp_create_nonce('wu_publish_pending_site')` is generated against that new session token. But the loopback receiver only sees the stale pre-login cookies, decodes a different (or empty) session token, and `wp_verify_nonce()` fails. Result: HTTP 400 / body `0`.

2. **Silent failure.** The caller only logs when `wp_remote_request` returns a `WP_Error`. A `400` response body `0` (the canonical AS nonce-failure signature) is just a successful HTTP transaction with the wrong body. No log file is written, no admin notice, nothing.

3. **`fastcgi_finish_request` polyfill detection is host-dependent.** Under FrankenPHP the function does not exist, so the caller sets `blocking => false`. That hides any HTTP-level signal anyway, because the caller never reads the response — even if we wanted to surface the `400`, we couldn't from this side.

When (1) trips, the fallback Action Scheduler entry is the only thing that publishes the site, which means site-creation latency becomes equal to "time until the next AS queue tick on the network main site." On installs with infrequent WP-cron pacing that latency can be tens of minutes.

## Proposed fix

Replace the cookie-based nonce with a server-side HMAC token that the calling process can mint without relying on `$_COOKIE` round-tripping, and surface non-2xx responses to the log.

**File to modify:** `inc/models/class-membership.php` (`publish_pending_site_async()` around line 2100)
**File to modify:** `inc/managers/class-membership-manager.php` (`publish_pending_site()` around line 111)

Suggested approach:

1. Introduce a short-lived (≤60s) HMAC token keyed on `wp_salt('auth') . $membership_id . $expires` minted by the caller:
   ```php
   $expires = time() + 60;
   $token   = hash_hmac('sha256', $this->get_id() . '|' . $expires, wp_salt('auth'));
   $rest_path = add_query_arg([
       'action'        => 'wu_publish_pending_site',
       'membership_id' => $this->get_id(),
       'wu_token'      => $token,
       'wu_expires'    => $expires,
   ], admin_url('admin-ajax.php'));
   ```
2. In `Membership_Manager::publish_pending_site()` replace `check_ajax_referer()` with:
   - If `wu_token` + `wu_expires` are present and verify with `hash_equals()` against the same HMAC, proceed.
   - Otherwise fall back to existing `check_ajax_referer('wu_publish_pending_site')` so the admin-modal/manual flow keeps working.
3. After `wp_remote_request()`, also log non-2xx responses (use `wp_remote_retrieve_response_code()`), so future loopback failures surface immediately:
   ```php
   if (is_wp_error($result)) {
       wu_log_add("membership-{$this->get_id()}", /* current message */);
   } else {
       $code = (int) wp_remote_retrieve_response_code($result);

## Out of scope

- Why AS queue runner only ticks hourly on a particular server — that is a stack-side WP-cron pacing issue, not a plugin bug. Tracked separately by the reporter.

title: ADR-001 Phase 3.5 — Port tenant-context call sites to network client (cross-repo companion)
body:
**ADR-001 Phase 3.5 — Port tenant-context call sites to network client (cross-repo companion)**

**Parent issue (full ADR context):** [Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy#43](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy/issues/43)
**ADR:** [adr-001-sovereign-tenant-isolation](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy/blob/main/docs/adr-001-sovereign-tenant-isolation.md)
**Audit:** [phase-3-tenant-context-audit.md](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy/blob/main/docs/phase-3-tenant-context-audit.md)

## Why this issue is in THIS repo

The 16 code-change PRs below all modify files in `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite` (this repo). The ADR + audit + endpoint catalogue + tenant client all live in `ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy`. This issue is the tracking hub for the per-PR work here.

## Goal

For every catalogued tenant-context call site (audit §2.6, §2.7, §3), wrap with a sovereignty branch:

```php
if ( defined( 'WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT' ) && WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT ) {
    $result = wu_mt_network_client()->some_method( $args );  // network REST
} else {
    $result = $existing_direct_db_query;                     // legacy fast path, unchanged
}
```

Tenant UI must be byte-for-byte identical between modes. Legacy mode untouched.

## PR breakdown (16 PRs, one logical group each)

Each PR title prefix: `ADR-001 Phase 3.5.<letter>:`. Each PR body references `Ref Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy#43` + this issue. Suggested merge order roughly follows letter sequence (a first; n/o/p can run parallel after b/d).

| PR | Scope | Files |
|---|---|---|
| a | Bootstrap: wire Settings_Prime fetch + `wu_get_setting` override | `inc/class-current.php` or new `inc/sovereign/class-sovereign-bootstrap.php` |
| b | Current resolution (Current::load_currents) | `inc/class-current.php` |
| c | UI Element reads (9 elements per audit §2.2) | `inc/ui/class-{account-summary,billing-info,current-membership,current-site,invoices,my-sites,subscription,tax,thank-you}-element.php` |
| d | Limit chain | `inc/managers/class-limitation-manager.php`, `inc/limits/class-{plugin,theme,customer-user-role,post-type,disk-space,site-template,trial}-limits.php` |
| e | Domain mapping in tenant context | `inc/class-domain-mapping.php`, `inc/domain-mapping/class-primary-domain.php` |
| f | Broadcast Manager | `inc/managers/class-broadcast-manager.php` |
| g | Visits Manager (batched flush via Visits_Batcher) | `inc/managers/class-visits-manager.php` |
| h | Site_Actions handlers (6 handlers, includes two-phase delete-site) | `inc/ui/class-site-actions-element.php` |
| i | Template_Switching_Element (long-running 202 + poll) | `inc/ui/class-template-switching-element.php` |
| j | Checkout flow (create_order, Cart, signup-fields) | `inc/checkout/class-{checkout,checkout-pages,cart,legacy-checkout}.php` |
| k | Gateway confirmations | `inc/managers/class-gateway-manager.php` |
| l | Domain_Mapping_Element CRUD | `inc/ui/class-domain-mapping-element.php` |
| m | Magic_Link consume | `inc/sso/class-magic-link.php` |
| n | Compat shims (Multiple_Accounts, Auto_Delete_Users, Edit_Users — decisions in #43) | `inc/compat/class-{multiple-accounts,auto-delete-users,edit-users}-compat.php` |
| o | Site model direct $wpdb writes | `inc/models/class-site.php` |
| p | Membership/Customer total_grossed | `inc/models/class-membership.php`, `inc/models/class-customer.php` |

## NOT touched (sovereignty exemptions)

Per audit §5.4, these MUST stay against network DB even in sovereign mode:

- `sunrise.php` → `Sunrise::run`, `Domain_Mapping::startup`, `Domain::get_by_domain` — run before tenant DB resolution.

Audit §1 row 25: `Gateway_Manager::maybe_process_webhooks` is `is_main_site()`-gated — out of tenant scope; do not touch.

## Per-PR verification

For each PR a-p:
1. With `WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT` defined: tenant-facing UI byte-identical to legacy mode (visual regression on one sovereign-test subsite, e.g. `sovereign-test.mygratis.site`).
2. With cache warm: tenant page load within 50ms of legacy fast path.
3. With cache cold: tenant page load issues exactly N HTTP calls (N = endpoints called by that page); verify via `WU_MT_API_DEBUG` log.
4. `WP_DEBUG` assertion: when `WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT` defined and ported call site fires, `$wpdb->dbh` never reaches network DB.
5. Legacy mode (`WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT` undefined) unchanged.
6. Tests for both branches.

## Sequencing dependencies

- PR a (settings prime) → unblocks reads in c, d.
- PR b (Current) → unblocks c, h.
- PR d (limits cached) → unblocks g (visit lock check).
- PR h, j (write handlers) need `wu_mt_network_client()` write methods deployed (multi-tenancy#39).

## Gate to start

- ⏳ multi-tenancy#31 (Phase 3.2 endpoint design) DONE.
- ⏳ multi-tenancy#35 (Phase 3.3 endpoints live on network).
- ⏳ multi-tenancy#39 (Phase 3.4 `wu_mt_network_client()` available in tenant).

Then PRs here can begin in dependency order.

## Status

Currently `status:blocked` on the three multi-tenancy gates above. Flip to `status:available` and dispatch PR a as soon as gates clear.

## Cross-repo coordination

- This issue is the tracking hub for the 16 PRs.
- Updates to `docs/phase-3-tenant-context-audit.md` (multi-tenancy) when a PR closes an audit row — strike-through or "ported in <PR>" annotation.
- Final closure: when all 16 PRs merge AND verification per PR passes, close this issue. The parent multi-tenancy#43 closes when this issue closes.

## Tier

tier:3 — coordination across 16 PRs; never auto-dispatch the parent. Individual PRs are tier:1 or tier:2 depending on scope.

title: ADR-001 Phase 3.5 — Sovereign-mode extension points, feature gates, and write branches
body:
**ADR-001 Phase 3.5 — Sovereign-mode extension points, feature gates, and write branches**

**ADR:** [adr-001-sovereign-tenant-isolation](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy/blob/main/docs/adr-001-sovereign-tenant-isolation.md)
**Audit:** [phase-3-tenant-context-audit.md](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy/blob/main/docs/phase-3-tenant-context-audit.md)
**Endpoint catalogue:** [phase-3-endpoints.md](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy/blob/main/docs/phase-3-endpoints.md)
**Cross-repo parent (ADR-side tracking):** Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy#43
**Tenant SDK companion:** Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy#39
**Supersedes:** #1248 (closed; original 16-PR plan, replaced by audit-grounded 7-PR plan)

## What this issue is

Sovereign tenants (per ADR-001 Phase 1) run in their own isolated DB with **no network DB credentials in memory**. They reach network state exclusively via signed REST calls to endpoints already shipped in `Sovereign_Tenant_Endpoints` (cross-repo PR landed 2026-05-21). This issue tracks the **upstream changes required to make WP Ultimo cooperate with sovereign mode** — extension points for the tenant SDK to hook, feature gates for incompatible code paths, and `if (SOVEREIGN)` branches for write paths that cannot be intercepted by filter.

All changes are gated on `defined('WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT') && WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT`. **Non-sovereign installs see zero behavioural change.**

## Sequencing into 7 PRs

### Track A — Filter chokepoints (unblocks SDK reads)

**PR-1: `Base_Model` `pre_*` filters** (~15 LOC)

File: `inc/models/class-base-model.php` (3 methods at lines 335-385).

```php
public static function get_by_id($item_id) {
    if (empty($item_id)) { return false; }
    $instance = new static();
    $pre = apply_filters("wu_pre_get_by_id_{$instance->model}", null, $item_id);
    if (null !== $pre) { return $pre; }
    $query_class = new $instance->query_class();
    return $query_class->get_item($item_id);
}
```

Same pattern for `get_by($column, $value)` (filter: `wu_pre_get_by_{$instance->model}`) and `get_by_hash($item_hash)` (filter: `wu_pre_get_by_hash_{$instance->model}`).

Verification: filter returns `null` → behaviour unchanged (existing test suite green). Filter returns a `Base_Model` instance → that instance is returned without invoking `$query_class->get_item()`.

Unblocks: ~30 caller sites for `Membership`, `Customer`, `Site`, `Domain`, `Payment`, `Broadcast`, `Product` via the helpers `wu_get_membership`, `wu_get_customer`, `wu_get_site`, `wu_get_domain`, `wu_get_payment`, `wu_get_broadcasts`, `wu_get_product`.

**PR-2: Per-method `pre_*` filters for 6 model methods that bypass the getters** (~50 LOC)

Each method gains a `wu_pre_{class}_{method}` filter at the top of its body. Filter returns `null` by default; non-null short-circuits the `$wpdb` call.

| File:line | Method | Filter name |
|---|---|---|
| `inc/models/class-site.php:1171` | `get_membership()` | `wu_pre_site_get_membership` |
| `inc/models/class-site.php:2255` | `get_all_by_type()` | `wu_pre_site_get_all_by_type` |
| `inc/models/class-site.php:2341` | `get_all_categories()` | `wu_pre_site_get_all_categories` |
| `inc/models/class-domain.php:641` | `get_by_site()` | `wu_pre_domain_get_by_site` |
| `inc/models/class-membership.php:2225` | `get_total_grossed()` | `wu_pre_membership_get_total_grossed` |
| `inc/models/class-customer.php:821` | `get_total_grossed()` | `wu_pre_customer_get_total_grossed` |

**NOT touched: `Domain::get_by_domain()` at `class-domain.php:704`.** Sunrise path — sovereignty exemption per audit §5.4. Already pre-empted by `Site_Registry` overlay in the tenancy plugin.

### Track B — Feature disables (no SDK dependency, parallelisable from day one)

**PR-3: Compat shim disables** (~15 LOC)

Three compat shims disabled in sovereign tenants because their feature semantics are incompatible with sovereign isolation:

| File | Reason |
|---|---|
| `inc/compat/class-auto-delete-users-compat.php` | Reads `wp_signups` (network-only); sovereign tenants don't host signup |
| `inc/compat/class-multiple-accounts-compat.php` | Cross-network identity sharing fundamentally breaks per-tenant `wp_users` isolation |
| `inc/compat/class-edit-users-compat.php` | Verify against audit — may need disable or may be safe via PR-1 model filters; decide during PR-3 design |

Pattern (one-line guard at top of each `init()`):

```php
public function init() {
    if ( defined( 'WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT' ) && WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT ) {
        return;
    }
    // ...existing init body...
}
```

**PR-4: Tenant-side Checkout disable + redirect** (~50 LOC)

Architectural decision: checkout always runs on the main site. Sovereign tenants are the *result* of a checkout, not its host.

Files:
- `inc/checkout/class-checkout.php` — AJAX handlers `wu_create_order` (:199), `wu_validate_form` (:206), `wu_check_user_exists` (:213), `wu_inline_login` (:220). Early-return in sovereign with error response pointing caller to main site.
- `inc/checkout/class-checkout-pages.php` — replace tenant checkout URLs with `network_site_url('/register/')` (or main-site-specific URL resolved from `get_network()->site_id`).
- `inc/checkout/class-cart.php` — guard model reads; class shouldn't instantiate in sovereign tenant context.
- `inc/checkout/class-legacy-checkout.php` — same.

UX requirement: existing tenant pages that previously rendered checkout forms or upgrade buttons must show a clear "Upgrade on main site" link instead of erroring.

**PR-5: Tenant-side Gateway_Manager disable** (~10 LOC)

File: `inc/managers/class-gateway-manager.php`.

- `process_gateway_confirmations` (:105) — early-return in sovereign.
- `ajax_check_payment_status` (:122) — early-return in sovereign.
- `maybe_process_webhooks` (:111) — **no change**, already `is_main_site()`-gated.

### Track C — Write branches (depends on tenant SDK 3.4.4 + 3.4.6)

**PR-6: Idempotent write branches for 8 paths** (~150 LOC)

Pattern per path:

```php
if ( defined( 'WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT' ) && WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT ) {
    $result = wu_mt_network_client()->{method_name}( ...$args );
    // map result to legacy return shape
    return $result;
}
// ...existing native body unchanged...
```

| File:line | Handler | SDK method (C-row endpoint) |
|---|---|---|
| `inc/ui/class-site-actions-element.php:668-682` | `handle_delete_site` (two-phase) | `delete_site_phase1` + `delete_site_phase2` / `delete_site_cancel` (C.1) |
| `inc/ui/class-site-actions-element.php:937-940` | `handle_change_email` | `change_customer_email` (C.2) |
| `inc/ui/class-site-actions-element.php` | `handle_change_password` | `change_customer_password` (C.10) |
| `inc/ui/class-site-actions-element.php:1342-1352` | `handle_cancel_membership` | `cancel_membership` (C.3) |
| `inc/ui/class-site-actions-element.php` | `handle_change_default_site` | `change_customer_primary_blog` (C.11) |
| `inc/ui/class-template-switching-element.php:138` | `switch_template` (async 202 + poll) | `switch_site_template` (C.4) |
| `inc/ui/class-domain-mapping-element.php` | add/remove domain | `add_site_domain` (C.8) / `remove_site_domain` (C.9) |
| `inc/sso/class-magic-link.php` | `handle_magic_link` (consume transient) | `consume_magic_link` (C.12) |

Each branch generates UUID v4 client-side (via SDK) for `Idempotency-Key`. Retries with the same UUID return cached server-side result; never re-invoke the operation.

**Out of scope for PR-6 (handled elsewhere):**

- `Maintenance_Mode::toggle_maintenance_mode` (:48) — already site-local (`wp_blogmeta` write); no change.
- `Visits_Manager::count_visits` (:43) — high-frequency; replaced by SDK `Visits_Batcher` 60s flush (tenancy repo issue #39 sub-task 3.4.5). The upstream call site becomes `wu_mt_network_client()->record_visit($blog_id)`.
- `Checkout::create_order` / signup flow writes — removed by PR-4 disable.
- `Gateway_Manager::process_gateway_confirmations` writes — removed by PR-5 disable.

**PR-7: Network-side webhook dispatcher + subscribe endpoint** (~120 LOC)

Network is the source of truth; sovereign tenants cache network state per Phase 3.3 endpoint TTLs. When network state changes, tenants need cache invalidation.

New file: `inc/sovereign/class-webhook-dispatcher.php`.

Hooks into:
- `wu_save_settings` → fire `settings.invalidate` to all subscribed sovereign tenants
- `wu_membership_post_save` → `membership.invalidate` (membership_id in payload) to subscribers caching that membership
- `wu_customer_post_save` → `customer.invalidate`
- `wu_domain_post_save` / `wu_domain_post_delete` → `domain.invalidate` (blog_id in payload)
- `wu_payment_post_save` → `payment.invalidate`
- `wu_broadcast_post_save` → `broadcasts.invalidate`

Plus subscribe/unsubscribe route on the existing `Sovereign_Tenant_Endpoints` namespace:

- `POST /webhook/subscribe` — body `{receiver_url, shared_secret_hash}`. Stores in network option `wu_mt_webhook_subscribers` keyed by blog_id.
- `POST /webhook/unsubscribe` — body `{blog_id}`.

Dispatcher signs each outbound POST with the per-tenant shared secret (HMAC-SHA256 over body). Tenant receiver (SDK 3.4.6) verifies.

Failure handling: failed delivery → retry once after 30s; on second failure, mark subscriber as `stale`. Tenant SDK detects staleness via the 5-minute polling fallback and re-subscribes on next request.

## Sequencing summary

```
PR-1 ──┐
       ├──> dev-main tag rc1 ──> tenancy SDK 3.4.3 wires dispatcher
PR-2 ──┘                         (tenancy issue #39)

PR-3 ─────  (parallel, no dependencies)
PR-4 ─────  (parallel, no dependencies)
PR-5 ─────  (parallel, no dependencies)

tenancy SDK 3.4.4 (writes) ──> PR-6 (write branches in this repo)
tenancy SDK 3.4.6 (receiver) ──> PR-7 (dispatcher in this repo)
```

Tracks A and B are entirely parallelisable from day one. Track C unblocks when the tenancy SDK reaches 3.4.4 / 3.4.6 milestones.

## Verification per PR

1. **Non-sovereign mode unchanged**: existing test suite green; non-sovereign tenant UI byte-identical (visual regression on a `legacy-test` subsite).
2. **Sovereign mode functional**: the corresponding read/write/disable succeeds against a sovereign-test subsite; `WP_DEBUG` assertion confirms `$wpdb->dbh` never reaches the network DB during the sovereign request.
3. **PR-3/4/5 (disables)**: features explicitly absent in sovereign tenant; admin gets clear "feature runs on main site only" messaging where the UI element used to render.
4. **PR-1/2 (filters)**: filter returns `null` → existing behaviour preserved (assertable via unit test); filter returns non-null → bypass succeeds.
5. **PR-6 (writes)**: idempotency replay (same UUID) returns identical response without re-invoking server-side operation.
6. **PR-7 (webhooks)**: network state change → subscribed sovereign tenant receives webhook within 5s; failed delivery → retry, then mark stale.

## Sovereignty exemptions (per audit §5.4)

These MUST stay against network DB even in sovereign mode — **do not** add `if (SOVEREIGN)` branches:

- `sunrise.php` → `Sunrise::run`, `Domain_Mapping::startup` — run before tenant DB resolution.
- `Domain::get_by_domain` (`class-domain.php:704`) — sunrise read; already pre-empted by tenancy plugin's `Site_Registry` overlay.

## Non-goals for this issue

- Tenant-side SDK implementation — tracked in `ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy#39`.
- Phase 4 legacy → sovereign migration — separate phase, depends on this issue + #39 complete.
- Cross-cutting CORS/capability audit of `wu/v2/*` REST routes — tracked separately in `ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy#67`.

## Branching strategy

Develop all 7 PRs on `dev-main` integration branch in this repo. Tag `dev-main-rc1` after PR-1 and PR-2 merge (unblocks tenancy SDK reads). Tag `dev-main-rc2` when PRs 3/4/5 merge. Tag `dev-main-rc3` (or final `dev-main`) when PRs 6/7 merge. Merge `dev-main` into `main` only when the tenancy SDK reaches its corresponding milestone and end-to-end verification passes against a real sovereign tenant.
