ADR-001 Phase 3.5 PR-2 — Per-method pre_* filters for 6 direct-wpdb model methods
body:
**ADR-001 Phase 3.5 PR-2 — Add `wu_pre_*` filters to 6 model methods that bypass the standard getters**

For #1250. Cross-repo parent: [Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy#43](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy/issues/43). Sibling: PR-1 (Base_Model getter filters).

## Goal

Six model methods perform direct `$wpdb` reads that bypass `Base_Model::get_by_id()` (which PR-1 makes filterable). Each needs its own pre-filter so the tenancy plugin can short-circuit them in sovereign tenants. Strictly additive — non-sovereign installs see zero behavioural change.

## Files and methods

| File:line | Method | New filter |
|---|---|---|
| `inc/models/class-site.php:1171` | `get_membership()` | `wu_pre_site_get_membership` |
| `inc/models/class-site.php:2255` | `get_all_by_type()` | `wu_pre_site_get_all_by_type` |
| `inc/models/class-site.php:2341` | `get_all_categories()` | `wu_pre_site_get_all_categories` |

title: ADR-001 Phase 3.5 PR-3 — Disable Auto_Delete_Users / Multiple_Accounts / Edit_Users compat in sovereign tenants
body:
**ADR-001 Phase 3.5 PR-3 — Disable incompatible compat shims in sovereign tenants**

For #1250. Cross-repo parent: [Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy#43](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy/issues/43).

## Goal

Three compat shims are semantically incompatible with sovereign isolation. Each gets an early-return guard in its `init()` method so it doesn't register hooks when `WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT` is defined. Non-sovereign installs see zero behavioural change.

## Files

| File | Reason for disable |
|---|---|
| `inc/compat/class-auto-delete-users-compat.php` | Reads `wp_signups` (network-only table); sovereign tenants don't host signup |
| `inc/compat/class-multiple-accounts-compat.php` | Rewrites `wp_users` JOINs across networks; fundamentally incompatible with per-tenant `wp_users` isolation |
| `inc/compat/class-edit-users-compat.php` | Verify against `docs/phase-3-tenant-context-audit.md` §2.1 — listed as a reader of `wp_sitemeta`; if its feature semantics need cross-network user editing, disable. If it's purely UI sugar that reads settings (covered by Settings_Prime), keep enabled. **Make the decision during PR design and document it in the PR body.** |

## Reference pattern

```php
public function init() {

    if ( defined( 'WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT' ) && WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT ) {
        return;
    }

    // ...existing init body unchanged...
}
```

If the class uses a constructor or singleton instead of `init()`, apply the same guard at the earliest hook-registration point. **Read the file first to choose the correct insertion point.**

## Verification

1. **Non-sovereign tenant:** features behave exactly as before (existing tests green, manual check on a legacy subsite).
2. **Sovereign tenant:** the compat shim's hooks are NOT registered. Test by asserting `has_action()` / `has_filter()` returns `false` for the shim's hook names in a sovereign-context bootstrap.
3. **No fatal errors:** loading the plugin in a sovereign tenant with these shims disabled must not break any other code path. Smoke-test a sovereign subsite's tenant frontend.

## UX consideration

For `Multiple_Accounts_Compat` and `Auto_Delete_Users_Compat`, super-admin may have these settings toggled on in network admin. The settings UI on the network is unaffected — these shims gate the *tenant-side* effects, not the network admin toggle. If a customer reports the feature "isn't working" on a sovereign tenant, that's expected and a future docs/UI improvement (out of scope for this PR).

## Branch

`dev-main` integration branch.

## LOC estimate

~15 lines total (3-5 lines per file).

## Tier

**tier:1** — trivial, well-scoped.

title: ADR-001 Phase 3.5 PR-4 — Disable tenant-side Checkout; redirect to main-site checkout
body: **ADR-001 Phase 3.5 PR-4 — Disable tenant-side Checkout in sovereign mode; redirect to main-site checkout** For #1250. Cross-repo parent: [Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy#43](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy/issues/43). ## Architectural decision **Checkout always runs on the main site.** Sovereign tenants are the *result* of a checkout, not its host. Tenant-side checkout AJAX, form rendering, cart, and signup-field validators are all disabled in sovereign tenants; users who land on a checkout URL inside a sovereign tenant are redirected to the main site's `/register/` page (or equivalent). This eliminates the largest single risk surface in the Phase 3.1 audit (§2.7.5: tenant-AJAX `wu_create_order` writing across `wu_payments`, `wu_customers`, `wu_memberships`, `wp_users` simultaneously) without porting any of that logic to REST. ## Files | File | Change | |---|---| | `inc/checkout/class-checkout.php` | Guard the 4 AJAX handlers at `:199-222` (`wu_create_order`, `wu_validate_form`, `wu_check_user_exists`, `wu_inline_login`). In sovereign context, return JSON error pointing caller to main-site checkout URL. | | `inc/checkout/class-checkout-pages.php` | When sovereign, replace tenant checkout/registration URLs with the main-site equivalent (resolve via `get_network()->site_id` → `get_blog_details( $main_site_id )->siteurl . '/register/'`). | | `inc/checkout/class-cart.php` | Guard model loading; the Cart class should not instantiate / hit the DB in a sovereign tenant context. | | `inc/checkout/class-legacy-checkout.php` | Same as `class-checkout.php` — guard hook registration. | ## Reference pattern For AJAX handlers: ```php public function wu_create_order() { if ( defined( 'WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT' ) && WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT ) { wp_send_json_error( [ 'code' => 'sovereign_checkout_disabled', 'message' => __( 'Checkout runs on the main site.', 'wp-ultimo' ), 'main_site_url' => $this->get_main_site_checkout_url(), ], 400 ); return; } // ...existing body... } ``` For URL replacement helper (new method on `Checkout_Pages`): ```php public function get_main_site_checkout_url(): string { $main_site = get_blog_details( get_network()->site_id ); if ( ! $main_site ) { return network_site_url( '/register/' ); } return trailingslashit( $main_site->siteurl ) . 'register/'; } ``` ## UX requirement Pages that previously rendered checkout forms or upgrade buttons inside sovereign tenants must render a clear "Upgrade on the main site" link instead of erroring or rendering an empty form. Wherever a checkout shortcode / block / element would render, replace its output in sovereign context with: ```html Upgrade your plan on the main site ``` Tenant admins and customers see a working link, not a broken form. ## Verification 1. **Non-sovereign tenant:** checkout works exactly as before. Existing E2E tests green. 2. **Sovereign tenant — AJAX:** `wu_create_order` POST returns `400 sovereign_checkout_disabled` with `main_site_url` in the response. 3. **Sovereign tenant — page render:** any URL that previously rendered a checkout form renders the "Upgrade on the main site" link with a working URL. 4. **Sovereign tenant — Cart class not instantiated:** confirm via debug log or unit test that `Cart::__construct` is never called during a sovereign tenant request. 5. **Main site:** checkout flow on the main site works unchanged. ## Branch `dev-main` integration branch. ## LOC estimate ~50 lines across 4 files, mostly guards + the URL helper. ## Tier **tier:2** — multi-file, requires UX decisions for the "Upgrade on main site" replacement element. --- [aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.17.27 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.15.7 with claude-haiku-4-5 spent 5h 48m and 38 tokens on this as a headless worker.

**ADR-001 Phase 3.5 PR-5 — Disable tenant-side `Gateway_Manager` in sovereign mode**

For #1250. Cross-repo parent: [Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy#43](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy/issues/43). Sibling: PR-4 (Checkout disable — same reasoning).

## Goal

Since checkout runs on the main site (PR-4), gateway return URLs and payment-status polling also land on the main site. The tenant-side `Gateway_Manager::process_gateway_confirmations` and `ajax_check_payment_status` should not fire in sovereign tenants.

## File

`inc/managers/class-gateway-manager.php`.

## Changes

| Method:line | Action |
|---|---|
| `process_gateway_confirmations()` :105 | Early-return when `defined( 'WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT' )`. Hook still registers but does nothing. |
| `ajax_check_payment_status()` :122 | Same. |

```php
public function process_gateway_confirmations() {
```

body: ## Goal Extend the sovereign-mode disable pattern (already established in `#1257` gateway-manager-disable, `#1258` compat-shims-disable, `#1261` checkout-disable) to the remaining customer-facing UI elements. When `defined('WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT')`, each listed element renders a single "Manage on main site" link instead of its normal output. Resolves §8 Q1 from ADR-001 Amendment 1 (downstream `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy#86`, #87). ## Files to modify Each of the following gets a sovereign-mode short-circuit in its `output()` method: | File | Element | |---|---| | `inc/ui/class-account-summary-element.php` | Account_Summary | | `inc/ui/class-billing-info-element.php` | Billing_Info | | `inc/ui/class-invoices-element.php` | Invoices | | `inc/ui/class-my-sites-element.php` | My_Sites | | `inc/ui/class-current-membership-element.php` | Subscription | | `inc/ui/class-current-site-element.php` | Current_Site (Site_Actions) | | `inc/ui/class-template-switching-element.php` | Template_Switching | | `inc/ui/class-domain-mapping-element.php` | Domain_Mapping | ## Elements that stay (do NOT touch) | File | Reason | |---|---| | `inc/ui/class-limits-element.php` | Reads from local `wp_blogmeta['wu_compiled_limits']` pushed by network — works fine in sovereign mode | | `inc/ui/class-site-maintenance-element.php` | Already site-local | | `inc/ui/class-login-form-element.php` | Reads from local `wp_options['wp-ultimo_v2_settings']` pushed by network — works fine | ## Pattern Follow the exact pattern from `#1261` (`inc/checkout/class-checkout.php` sovereign-mode short-circuit) and `#1257` (`inc/managers/class-gateway-manager.php`). At the top of each element's `output()` method: ```php public function output($atts) { if (defined('WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT')) { return wu_get_template_contents( 'elements/sovereign-redirect', [ 'main_site_account_url' => $this->get_main_site_account_url(), 'element_label' => __('Your account', 'wp-ultimo'), ] ); } // ...existing rendering... } ``` ## New template | File | Purpose | |---|---| | `views/elements/sovereign-redirect.php` | Tiny template that renders ` → `. ~10 LOC. | ## New helper | File | Purpose | |---|---| | `inc/functions/sovereign.php` | `wu_mt_main_site_account_url(): string` — returns `get_admin_url($main_site_blog_id, 'admin.php?page=account&return_to=' . urlencode(home_url('/wp-admin/')))`. ~20 LOC. The receiving page is modified in 3-A8 to handle the `return_to` query arg. | ## Tests - For each modified element, add a unit test: in sovereign mode (`define('WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT', true)`), `output()` returns the redirect template output, not the element's normal rendering. - Regression test: in non-sovereign mode, behaviour is unchanged. ## Reference patterns - `#1257` merge commit `2da29b30`: sovereign-mode short-circuit in `Gateway_Manager` - `#1258` merge commit `5d6cdd6c`: sovereign-mode disable of compat shims - `#1261` merge commit `4ddd67e1`: sovereign-mode disable of tenant-side Checkout Follow the established style and quality bar. ## Verification 1. Enable sovereign mode on a test tenant; visit each customer-panel page in tenant `/wp-admin/`; verify each element renders the redirect link. 2. On a non-sovereign tenant, all elements still render normally. 3. `wp ultimo:tests run` (or equivalent) passes including the new element tests. 4. PHPStan / Phan / qlty pass. ## ADR context ADR-001 Amendment 1 §4.3 "PR-B Part remaining (3-A7)" + §8 resolved Q1 + §11 decision log. ## Tier Tier:2 — 8 element files + 1 template + 1 helper; pattern is established but quantity is non-trivial. title: ADR-001 Phase 3-A8 — Modify ?page=account to serve sovereign-tenant customers on main site
body:
## Goal

Modify the existing customer-facing `?page=account` admin page (and sibling customer-panel pages) so it works on the **main site** for sovereign-tenant customers. Today it expects to render inside the customer's own subsite; under ADR-001 Amendment 1 (downstream `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy#86`, #87), sovereign-tenant customers visit it on the main-site domain instead.

**No new admin pages** — modify, don't replace. This resolves §8 Q3 (PR #87).

## Files to modify

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `inc/admin-pages/customer-panel/class-account-admin-page.php` | (1) Drop the "current site is the customer's site" assumption — derive customer context from `wp_get_current_user()` instead. (2) Accept optional `?return_to=<url>` query arg; if present, render a "Back to your site" link that points at the return URL. (3) Ensure capability gates work for main-site context (current customer caps should already work; verify). |
| `inc/admin-pages/customer-panel/class-my-sites-admin-page.php` | Same three changes; "My Sites" lists the customer's sites across the network including sovereign tenants, each linking to its own domain (not back to a `?blog_id=` switch). |
| `inc/admin-pages/customer-panel/class-template-switching-admin-page.php` | Same changes; template-switching action targets a specific site, identified via a query arg or selector rather than `get_current_blog_id()`. |
| `inc/admin-pages/customer-panel/class-checkout-admin-page.php` | If checkout is reached from a sovereign-tenant context, ensure the return-to-tenant flow works. |
| `inc/admin-pages/customer-panel/class-add-new-site-admin-page.php` | Sovereign-tenant customers should be able to add additional sites; verify no regressions for the main-site context. |

## Return-to-tenant flow

When a sovereign-tenant customer clicks "Manage on main site" (from 3-A7 redirects), the URL is:

```
https://main-site.example/wp-admin/admin.php?page=account&return_to=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-tenant.example%2Fwp-admin%2F
```

The account page renders normally; somewhere in the page header (or footer) it includes a prominent "← Back to {tenant-site-name}" link pointing at the decoded `return_to` URL. The link uses Phase 2 SSO so the customer doesn't have to re-authenticate.

`return_to` must be validated: only URLs whose host matches a known sovereign tenant of the current customer are accepted; anything else falls back to no link.

## "Current site" assumption removal

Existing code patterns to find and fix:

```php
$current_site = wu_get_current_site();           // assumes the user is browsing their own site
$blog_id      = get_current_blog_id();           // assumes that's the customer's site
$current_user = wp_get_current_user();
$membership   = $current_user->get_membership(); // may need to switch to membership-driven context
```

Replace "current site" with "current customer's primary site" or "the site identified by the URL query arg" (e.g. `?site_id=42` for multi-site customers).

## Reference patterns

- `wp_get_current_user()` and the customer model lookup pattern: see existing `Customer::get_by_user_id()` in `inc/models/class-customer.php`.
- Phase 2 SSO token issue: downstream `inc/network/class-auth-token-manager.php` — the main site mints an SSO token, the tenant validates it. The `return_to` link should include the SSO token in its URL query.
- Existing customer-panel pages already handle main-site context for some operations; this issue brings the rest of the pages into line.

## Verification

1. From a sovereign tenant, click "Manage on main site" on the Account_Summary element (added in 3-A7); verify you land on `https://main-site/wp-admin/admin.php?page=account` with the customer's data visible.
2. The "← Back to {tenant}" link is present and points at the original tenant URL via SSO.
3. From the main site, the same page renders normally for non-sovereign customers (no regression).
4. A malicious `?return_to=https://evil.example/` falls back to no link (validation rejects unknown hosts).
5. Multi-site customers see all their sites in My_Sites including sovereign tenants, each linking to its own domain.

## ADR context

ADR-001 Amendment 1 §4.3 "PR-C" + §8 resolved Q3 + §11 decision log.

## Tier

Tier:2 — five admin pages, return-URL flow, SSO integration, validation.

title: SSO: /sso-grant URL produced by getAttachUrl() is no longer routed
body:
## Summary

`SSO_Broker::getAttachUrl()` produces URLs of the form
`<main_site>/sso-grant?...`, but no request to `/sso-grant` ever
reaches a usable handler on the main site. After #1297 nothing in
core uses that URL anymore, but `getAttachUrl()` is still on the
public API of the broker and any third-party caller of it will
silently 404.

## Where the routing dies

In `inc/sso/class-sso.php::handle_requests()` the dispatcher pulls
`$action` from the path (so `/sso-grant` yields `sso_grant`) and then
fires:

```php
do_action( "wu_sso_handle_{$action}_grant", ... );
```

For `/sso-grant` that produces `wu_sso_handle_sso_grant_grant` — an
action with no listener. For `/sso` it produces
`wu_sso_handle_sso_grant`, which **is** registered and routes to
`handle_server()`. So `/sso` works; `/sso-grant` is dead.

## Reproduction

```
curl -i 'https://<main_site>/sso-grant?broker=foo&token=bar&checksum=baz'
```

…returns whatever the front-end of the main site happens to render
for an unknown URL (usually 404 or the home page), not the SSO
server response.

## Suggested fixes (pick one)

1. **Remove `getAttachUrl()` / the `/sso-grant` URL entirely.** After
   #1297 nothing internal uses it. Document the magic-link flow as
   the only entry point.
2. **Normalise the dispatcher** so `/sso-grant` is rewritten to
   `/sso` (or so both fire `wu_sso_handle_sso_grant`). This keeps
   the public method working for downstream consumers that may have
   started calling it.

Option 1 is cleaner; option 2 is more conservative for anyone who
has integrated against `getAttachUrl()` already.

## Context

Discovered while diagnosing the front-end auto-SSO regression fixed
in #1297. Mentioned in that PR's "Out of scope" section but tracked
here for follow-up.

title: SSO: should_skip_redirect_due_to_loop() over-counts on non-SSO requests
body:
## Summary

`should_skip_redirect_due_to_loop()` (added in #1203) increments the
`wu_sso_redirect_attempts` cookie on **every** logged-out call to
`handle_auth_redirect()`, regardless of whether the previous request
was itself part of an SSO loop. As a result the counter can burn
through its budget on benign repeat visits — e.g. a logged-out user
who refreshes `/wp-admin/` a few times, or any caller that hits an
auth-protected URL without ever entering the SSO flow.

Once the counter trips, real SSO attempts are then suppressed for
the cooldown window even though no loop ever occurred.

## Where

`inc/sso/class-sso.php::should_skip_redirect_due_to_loop()` /
`handle_auth_redirect()` (post-#1203). The counter is bumped before
any check that the current request actually came from an SSO hop.

## Suggested fix

Scope the increment to requests whose `Referer` is the main-site
`/sso*` endpoint (or whose URL carries one of the SSO query params:
`wu_sso_token`, `sso=login`, `return_url`, `_jsonp`). A request with
no SSO fingerprint is not a loop iteration and should not consume
the budget.

Pseudo-code:

```php
$referer  = wp_get_referer();
$is_sso_hop =
    ( $referer && false !== strpos( $referer, '/sso' ) )
    || wu_request( 'wu_sso_token' )
    || wu_request( 'sso' ) === 'login'
    || wu_request( '_jsonp' );

if ( ! $is_sso_hop ) {
    return false; // not part of a loop; don't count, don't skip
}
```

## Context

Surfaced while diagnosing the front-end auto-SSO regression fixed
in #1297. Mentioned in that PR's "Out of scope" section but tracked
here for follow-up.

title: fix(membership): invalidate wu_membership_meta cache when pending_site is deleted
body:
# fix(membership): invalidate wu_membership_meta cache when pending_site is deleted

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-05-28
- **Session:** opencode interactive (tgc.church / mygratis.site multisite ops)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (reviewer-of-record: superdav42)
- **Conversation context:** Free-checkout flow on `sdaiagent.com` was stuck on "Creating your site…" indefinitely after the background publish finished. Root cause: `Membership::delete_pending_site()` (`inc/models/class-membership.php:2299-2302`) deletes the meta row but the persistent object-cache entry under `wu_membership_meta` keeps the original `Site` object alive across the FPM worker boundary, so the frontend AJAX poll `wu_check_pending_site_created` (`inc/managers/class-membership-manager.php:205`) keeps seeing a pending site forever. A downstream mu-plugin shim at priority 5 (`ai_agent_bust_pending_site_cache` in `tgc.church/site/web/app/mu-plugins/ai-agent-checkout-thankyou.php`) plugs the gap; this brief is the upstream fix so the shim can be retired.

## What

In `Membership::delete_pending_site()`, explicitly invalidate the `wu_membership_meta` object-cache entry for the current membership immediately after `delete_meta('pending_site')`. Behaviour change: a successful or failed `delete_meta` call still triggers a `wp_cache_delete( $this->get_id(), 'wu_membership_meta' )`. This is purely defensive — WordPress's `delete_metadata()` does call `wp_cache_delete` internally, but only when at least one row was deleted; in the cross-process publish flow that guarantee does not hold (see ## Critical Context).

## Why

- **Reproducible failure mode** (verified against production `mygratis.site` release `20260528172900`): pending-site polling loop runs forever after `async_publish_pending_site` completes, until `wp cache flush` is run manually OR a `wp_cache_delete( $membership_id, 'wu_membership_meta' )` is fired ahead of UM's AJAX handler.
- The background `async_publish_pending_site` runs in a separate FPM worker (it's triggered via HTTP loopback in `Membership::publish_pending_site_async`). Whatever invalidation WordPress core does on the background worker's local + persistent-cache copy of `wu_membership_meta` does not always propagate to the polling worker's in-memory copy in time for the next 5-second poll. Docket Cache (the production object cache here) has a small staleness window for cross-process invalidations.
- A one-line belt-and-braces `wp_cache_delete` in the model method closes the window with zero behavioural risk: the only effect is that the next `get_metadata('wu_membership', $id, 'pending_site')` call hits the DB instead of stale cache.
- Without this fix, every consumer hitting Docket Cache (or any persistent object cache with similar cross-process semantics) has to ship its own shim. We already are.

## Tier

`tier:1` — single-line addition to one method, with a clear narrowly-scoped purpose. No design decisions. Model required: **opus-4-7** per the model policy in `tgc.church/site/web/app/plugins/ultimate-multisite-multi-tenancy/AGENTS.md` (this PR interfaces with upstream `Membership` model contract, meta API, and the object-cache surface — exactly the class of upstream-contract work the policy is for).

## Files to Modify

- `EDIT: inc/models/class-membership.php:2293-2302` — augment `delete_pending_site()` with explicit cache invalidation.

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1 — Edit `Membership::delete_pending_site()`

Current implementation:

```php
	/**
	 * Removes a pending site of a membership.
	 *
	 * @since 2.0.0
	 * @return bool
	 */
	public function delete_pending_site() {

		return $this->delete_meta('pending_site');
	}
```

Replace with:

```php
	/**
	 * Removes a pending site of a membership.
	 *
	 * Also explicitly invalidates the `wu_membership_meta` object-cache
	 * entry for this membership. WordPress's `delete_metadata()` calls
	 * `wp_cache_delete()` internally, but only after a successful row
	 * delete and only against the current process's cache. In the
	 * cross-process publish flow (background `async_publish_pending_site`
	 * runs in a separate FPM worker from the frontend AJAX poll
	 * `wu_check_pending_site_created`), the polling worker's in-memory
	 * copy of `wu_membership_meta` outlives the invalidation, and
	 * persistent object caches (e.g. Docket Cache) have a small
	 * cross-process staleness window. Without this explicit delete,
	 * the AJAX poll keeps reading a non-null `pending_site` from cache
	 * forever and the thank-you page is stuck on "Creating your site…"
	 * until `wp cache flush` is run manually.
	 *
	 * @since 2.0.0
	 * @return bool
	 */
	public function delete_pending_site() {

		$result = $this->delete_meta('pending_site');

		wp_cache_delete($this->get_id(), 'wu_membership_meta');

		return $result;
	}
```

Note: WordPress core's `delete_metadata()` uses the `<meta_type>_meta` cache-group naming convention, so `wu_membership_meta` is the correct group for this model (`get_meta_type_name()` returns `'wu_membership'`). Verify by reading `inc/models/class-base-model.php:815-824` (`delete_meta()`) and tracing to the WordPress core `delete_metadata()` source (`wp-includes/meta.php`).

### Step 2 — PHPCS compliance check

This repo enforces WordPress Coding Standards (`AGENTS.md` Code Style section). The added line uses Yoda-friendly call form, single quotes, and tab indentation — should pass without changes. Run:

```bash
vendor/bin/phpcs inc/models/class-membership.php
# If violations appear, auto-fix and re-read before any further edit:
vendor/bin/phpcbf inc/models/class-membership.php || true
```

(`phpcbf` exits 1 on successful fixes — see `AGENTS.md` "Common bash:other Failures".)

## Verification

```bash

php -l inc/models/class-membership.php

# 2. PHPStan (level 0 per phpstan.neon.dist)
vendor/bin/phpstan analyse inc/models/class-membership.php

# 3. Unit-test regression: existing Membership tests must still pass
vendor/bin/phpunit --filter Membership_Test

# 4. Targeted assertion — call delete_pending_site then assert
#    wp_cache_get returns false for the meta group:
#    Add (or extend an existing) test in tests/WP_Ultimo/Models/Membership_Test.php
#    Skeleton:
```

```php
public function test_delete_pending_site_invalidates_meta_cache() {
	$membership = wu_create_membership(/* ... */);
	$membership->update_meta('pending_site', (object) ['id' => 1]);
	// Warm the cache.
	get_metadata('wu_membership', $membership->get_id());
	$this->assertNotFalse(wp_cache_get($membership->get_id(), 'wu_membership_meta'));
	$membership->delete_pending_site();
	$this->assertFalse(wp_cache_get($membership->get_id(), 'wu_membership_meta'));
}
```

```bash
# 5. Production-equivalent smoke test (requires a Docket-Cache-style persistent
#    cache + a multi-process flow). Easiest reproduction:
#    a. Wire UM up with Docket Cache or W3 Total Cache object-cache.
#    b. Trigger the free-checkout flow end-to-end.
#    c. After payment, watch the thank-you page poll wu_check_pending_site_created.
#    d. Without this patch: poller returns 'running' indefinitely after publish.
#       With this patch: poller returns 'completed' on the first poll after publish.
#    Reference downstream reproduction: tgc.church free-checkout on sdaiagent.com,
#    membership 59 / blog 88 / e2e-test-1779988090.sdaiagent.com (resolved by
#    mu-plugin shim that does exactly this wp_cache_delete; this PR moves it upstream).
```

## Files Scope

- `inc/models/class-membership.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Models/Membership_Test.php` (if adding the regression test)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Membership::delete_pending_site()` calls `wp_cache_delete( $this->get_id(), 'wu_membership_meta' )` after `delete_meta('pending_site')` and before returning.
- [ ] Return value is unchanged (`bool` from `delete_meta()`).
- [ ] Existing `Membership_Test` PHPUnit class passes without modification.
- [ ] New regression test asserts cache entry is `false` after `delete_pending_site()` even when warmed beforehand (or an existing test is extended with the same assertion).
- [ ] PHPCS clean: `vendor/bin/phpcs inc/models/class-membership.php` exits 0.
- [ ] PHPStan clean: `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse inc/models/class-membership.php` reports no new errors.
- [ ] PR title uses Conventional Commits: `fix(membership):` prefix.
- [ ] PR body cites the cross-process Docket Cache failure mode and includes the reproduction recipe.

## Critical Context

- **WordPress core does invalidate — but not reliably across processes.** `delete_metadata()` in `wp-includes/meta.php` calls `wp_cache_delete( $object_id, $meta_type . '_meta' )` after a successful row delete. Two conditions break the invalidation guarantee for this flow:
  1. The background `async_publish_pending_site` runs in a different FPM worker from the frontend AJAX poller. Process-local in-memory cache in the poller is not invalidated by the background process's `wp_cache_delete`. Persistent backends (Docket Cache) have a small disk-mtime-based staleness window.
  2. If `delete_pending_site()` is ever called twice in rapid succession (e.g., async publish path + a cron retry path), the second call's `delete_metadata()` finds no rows and returns false BEFORE running `wp_cache_delete`, so any stale cache entry written between the two deletes (by a parallel `get_metadata` call) survives.
  The explicit `wp_cache_delete` covers both.
- **Production-validated downstream patch:** `tgc.church/site/web/app/mu-plugins/ai-agent-checkout-thankyou.php:743-773` does exactly this `wp_cache_delete` at AJAX-handler priority 5 (ahead of UM's priority 10) and resolves the failure end-to-end. The fix in this PR moves it inside the model so it doesn't need an AJAX-handler shim.
- **No behavioural change for non-persistent-cache deployments.** With WP's default non-persistent object cache, `wp_cache_delete` is a no-op against an already-cleared key. Net effect for those sites is zero.
- **Why not call `clean_metadata_cache`?** WordPress core does not export a public `clean_metadata_cache` for arbitrary meta types — it's per-type (`clean_post_cache`, `clean_user_cache`, etc.). `wp_cache_delete( $object_id, $meta_type . '_meta' )` is the canonical pattern (it's literally what `delete_metadata` itself does).
- **Why not also flush after `update_pending_site`?** `update_meta()` → `update_metadata()` already invalidates on write, and the polling failure mode is specifically deletion-after-publish. Keep this PR minimal; do not expand scope.
- **No PR-level CI**, and the downstream tgc.church reviewer-of-record (superdav42) will validate. Validate against the documented reproduction recipe before approving.

## Relevant Files (upstream verification)

- `inc/models/class-membership.php:2293-2302` — `delete_pending_site()` (the only edit).
- `inc/models/class-membership.php:62` — `const META_PENDING_SITE = 'pending_site';` (confirms key name).
- `inc/models/class-membership.php:2089-2092` — `get_pending_site()` (the read path the cache invalidation guards).
- `inc/models/class-base-model.php:815-824` — `delete_meta()` → `delete_metadata()`.
- `inc/managers/class-membership-manager.php:205-265` — `check_pending_site_created()` AJAX handler (the consumer that depends on this fix).
- `inc/managers/class-membership-manager.php:166-193` — `async_publish_pending_site()` (the writer that triggers `delete_pending_site()` from a separate FPM worker via HTTP loopback in `publish_pending_site_async`).
- Downstream reference (production-validated): `tgc.church/site/web/app/mu-plugins/ai-agent-checkout-thankyou.php:743-773`.

## Dependencies

- **Blocks:** removal of `ai_agent_bust_pending_site_cache` from `tgc.church/site/web/app/mu-plugins/ai-agent-checkout-thankyou.php` once this lands and deploys.

title: feat(sso): add wu_sso_url filter to wu_with_sso() helper
body:
<!-- #auto-dispatch -->

## Problem

`wu_with_sso( $url )` (`inc/functions/domain.php:133`) returns the SSO-decorated URL with no `apply_filters()` hook, leaving downstream tenancy plugins unable to substitute the URL when the target site needs a different SSO transport.

Sibling helper `Magic_Link::generate_magic_link()` already exposes `apply_filters( 'wu_magic_link_url', $magic_link, $user_id, $site_id, $redirect_to )` at line 148 of `inc/sso/class-magic-link.php`, and downstream consumers (e.g. `Ultimate_Multisite_Multi_Tenancy\Users\Sovereign_SSO::maybe_replace_url_for_sovereign()`) already register against it successfully — so the precedent and shape are already established. The missing `wu_sso_url` filter is the only piece preventing the equivalent override on the `wu_with_sso()` path.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `wu_with_sso( $url )` returns through `apply_filters( 'wu_sso_url', $url, $user, $site_id, $redirect_to )`, matching the four-arg pattern of `wu_magic_link_url`.
2. Default behaviour unchanged when no filter is attached: `wu_with_sso( $url )` returns exactly what `\WP_Ultimo\SSO\SSO::with_sso( $url )` returns today.
3. Filter receives best-available context:
   - `$user` — current user object (`wp_get_current_user()`), or `null` if no user resolvable.
   - `$site_id` — target blog ID parsed from the URL host via `get_blog_id_from_url()` if resolvable, else `0`.
   - `$redirect_to` — empty string by default (callers who need a richer signature can wire an enhanced helper later).
4. Inline docblock on the new filter mirrors the style/granularity of `wu_magic_link_url`'s docblock (lines 138-147 of `class-magic-link.php`).
5. No changes to `\WP_Ultimo\SSO\SSO::with_sso()` itself — keep the filter at the public `wu_*` helper boundary so internal callers that use the class directly remain unfiltered (preserves current internal semantics).

## Reference pattern

`inc/sso/class-magic-link.php:138-148` — existing `wu_magic_link_url` filter docblock + `apply_filters()` call. Mirror the docblock structure, `@since` tag, and parameter ordering.

## Files

- `inc/functions/domain.php:133-136` — `wu_with_sso()` body. Add filter at return.

## Verification

```php
// Round-trip on host network:
add_filter( 'wu_sso_url', function ( $url, $user, $site_id, $redirect_to ) {
    return $url . '#test-filter-fired';
}, 10, 4 );

echo wu_with_sso( 'https://example.com/' );
// Expect trailing #test-filter-fired
```

Verify default (no filter attached) `wu_with_sso( 'https://example.com/' )` returns the same string as `\WP_Ultimo\SSO\SSO::with_sso( 'https://example.com/' )`.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT modify `\WP_Ultimo\SSO\SSO::with_sso()` internals.
- Do NOT change `wu_with_sso()`'s function signature (still single `$url` arg).
- Do NOT add the filter at additional call sites (e.g. inside `SSO::with_sso()`); scope is the public wrapper only.

## Notes

Filing on behalf of UM-MT `Sovereign_SSO` (`inc/users/class-sovereign-sso.php:74-76`, shipped in UM-MT PR #157, merged 2026-05-28), which already registers `add_filter( 'wu_sso_url', [ __CLASS__, 'maybe_replace_url_for_sovereign' ], 10, 4 )` against the not-yet-existing filter. The `wu_magic_link_url` half of that pair is fully live and verified working for sovereign tenants on production today.

title: fix(membership): invalidate wu_membership_meta in pending-site poll handler (cross-worker cache coherence; UM #1308 follow-up)
body:
<!-- #auto-dispatch -->

## Problem

PR #1308 (merged 2026-05-28) adds `wp_cache_delete( $this->get_id(), 'wu_membership_meta' )` inside `Membership::delete_pending_site()` to invalidate the persistent (Docket) cache and the **calling worker's** in-process `WP_Object_Cache`. That fix is necessary but **not sufficient** when the publish loopback and the polling AJAX are handled by different long-lived PHP workers (FrankenPHP worker mode, php-fpm with high `pm.max_requests`, php-pm, RoadRunner, etc.).

**Verified failure on production (`tgc.church`, payment `JJJ3D4416E`, membership 61, blog 90, 2026-05-29 02:08 UTC)**:

1. Browser loads thank-you page. Worker B handles the first poll, calls `$membership->get_pending_site()`, populates `wu_membership_meta` cache for the membership ID in Worker B's in-process `WP_Object_Cache`.
2. Worker A handles the async `publish_pending_site_async()` loopback (`admin-ajax.php?action=wu_publish_pending_site`). After the site is created, `delete_pending_site()` deletes the DB row and runs `wp_cache_delete()` per PR #1308 — clearing Worker A's in-process cache and Docket's disk cache.
3. Browser polls every 5s. Worker affinity keeps routing polls to Worker B. Worker B's in-process cache still holds the pending Site object. `get_pending_site()` returns truthy indefinitely. Thank-you page stuck on "Creating your site…" forever.
4. `wp cache flush` unsticks it (Docket broadcasts flush to all workers).

DB state at the moment of the stuck-poll diagnosis:

```
wp_wu_membershipmeta WHERE wu_membership_id = 61:
  (single row) verified_payment_discount = 1
  (no pending_site row — delete_pending_site DID run)

$membership->get_pending_site()  → still returns a Site object (stale Worker B cache)
$membership->get_pending_site()  → false   ← after `wp cache flush`
```

PR #1308 cannot fix this on its own because there is no IPC mechanism in WP's object-cache contract to broadcast invalidation across PHP worker processes. Each long-lived worker holds an independent in-process mirror of what it has read.

## Proposed fix

Move the cache invalidation into **the read path that polls for completion** — `wp_ajax_wu_check_pending_site_created` (`inc/managers/class-membership-manager.php:205`) — instead of (or in addition to) the write path. That handler runs in the polling worker's request context, so the `wp_cache_delete` it performs invalidates the only worker whose stale cache is actually blocking the user.

The minimal change is one line at the top of the AJAX handler, before it calls `$membership->get_pending_site()`:

```php
// Cross-process invalidation: the publish loopback runs in a different
// long-lived worker, and PR #1308's wp_cache_delete in delete_pending_site()
// only invalidates that worker's in-process cache plus the persistent store.
// We force this poller worker to re-read from the (already-fresh) persistent
// store / DB on every poll, so workers that warmed the meta cache before
// delete_pending_site() fired stop returning stale 'still pending' results.
wp_cache_delete( $membership->get_id(), 'wu_membership_meta' );
```

This is what downstream `tgc.church` already does via a mu-plugin shim (`ai_agent_bust_pending_site_cache`, attached at priority 5 ahead of UM's default 10). Folding the same logic upstream lets every UM consumer benefit without a custom mu-plugin.

## Acceptance criteria

1. In `Membership_Manager::handle_check_pending_site_created()` (or whichever method backs `wp_ajax_wu_check_pending_site_created`), invalidate `wu_membership_meta` for the resolved membership ID **before** calling `get_pending_site()` / `get_sites()`. Use `wp_cache_delete( $membership->get_id(), 'wu_membership_meta' )`.
2. Behaviour when no persistent cache is active: no observable change (`wp_cache_delete` on an empty key is a no-op).
3. Behaviour when Docket / Redis / memcached is active and `delete_pending_site()` has already run on another worker: this poller returns the fresh DB state immediately.
4. Behaviour when `delete_pending_site()` has NOT yet run: this poller still reads `pending_site` correctly — the cache repopulates on the SQL read.
5. Performance: one extra `wp_cache_delete` per poll (one cache key, network-light for Redis/memcached, single `unlink` for Docket). At the 5s polling cadence this is negligible (≤12 cache deletes per minute per active checkout).
6. Add a regression test in `tests/WP_Ultimo/Managers/Membership_Manager_Test.php` (or wherever the existing AJAX handler tests live) that:
   - Warms `wu_membership_meta` cache with a stale pending Site for membership N.
   - Calls the handler directly (or via `do_action( 'wp_ajax_wu_check_pending_site_created' )`).
   - Asserts the response reports `completed` (or whatever signals "no pending site") rather than the stale pending state.

## Files

- `inc/managers/class-membership-manager.php` (one `wp_cache_delete` call near the top of the AJAX handler).
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Managers/Membership_Manager_Test.php` (one new test method, ~25 LOC).

## Reference pattern

The downstream shim that currently works around this in production:

```php
// tgc.church/site/web/app/mu-plugins/ai-agent-checkout-thankyou.php
add_action( 'wp_ajax_wu_check_pending_site_created', 'ai_agent_bust_pending_site_cache', 5 );
add_action( 'wp_ajax_nopriv_wu_check_pending_site_created', 'ai_agent_bust_pending_site_cache', 5 );

function ai_agent_bust_pending_site_cache(): void {
    if ( ! function_exists( 'wu_get_membership_by_hash' ) ) return;
    $hash = isset( $_REQUEST['membership_hash'] ) ? sanitize_text_field( wp_unslash( $_REQUEST['membership_hash'] ) ) : '';
    if ( empty( $hash ) ) return;
    $membership = wu_get_membership_by_hash( $hash );
    if ( ! $membership ) return;
    wp_cache_delete( $membership->get_id(), 'wu_membership_meta' );
}
```

The upstream version just needs the `wp_cache_delete()` line; membership resolution is already done by UM's handler.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT add cross-process IPC, transient-based broadcasting, or generation counters. This is an unbounded refactor; the polling-side invalidation handles the specific case cheaply.
- Do NOT remove or weaken PR #1308's `wp_cache_delete` in `delete_pending_site()`. That fix is correct for the within-process and persistent-store cases; this PR is an additional fix for the cross-process case.
- Do NOT touch the publish path (`publish_pending_site`, `publish_pending_site_async`). The bug is purely in the read path's cache freshness.

## Verification

After applying the fix on `tgc.church` production:

```bash
# Simulate the stuck state: warm Worker B's cache with stale pending_site.
wp --url=$NETWORK eval '
    wp_cache_delete( 61, "wu_membership_meta" );
    $m = wu_get_membership( 61 );
    $m->get_pending_site();   // warms cache with current DB value
'

# In a separate session, delete the DB row directly without touching cache:
wp --url=$NETWORK db query "DELETE FROM wp_wu_membershipmeta WHERE wu_membership_id=61 AND meta_key='pending_site'"

# Hit the AJAX handler — must report completed, NOT pending.
curl "https://$NETWORK/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=wu_check_pending_site_created&membership_hash=$HASH"
# Expect: {"publish_status":"completed",...}
# Without the fix: {"publish_status":"pending",...}
```

## Notes

Downstream tracking: `tgc.church` retired its `ai_agent_bust_pending_site_cache` shim in commit `16a2fde9` after PR #1308 deployed, then immediately re-restored it in commit `8a6ebbef` when the production failure recurred. The retirement assumed #1308 was sufficient; the failure mode documented here proves it is not. The downstream shim is now back in place with a block comment pointing to this issue.

Filed during post-deploy production verification, 2026-05-29.

title: test(e2e): re-enable 010-manual-checkout-flow.spec.js (regression since PR #1280)
body:
## Summary

`tests/e2e/cypress/integration/010-manual-checkout-flow.spec.js` has been failing on every `main` e2e run since PR #1280 (commit `57176437`, 2026-05-26) wired it into CI for the first time. The form submission on `/register/` never reaches `status=done`, and the verification fixture sees `um_payment_status: 'no-payments'` because no payment row is created.

The spec is temporarily disabled in `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` (see the `TODO(#NNN)` comment in the `Run Checkout Tests (After Setup)` step) so it stops blocking unrelated PRs. This issue tracks restoring it.

## Symptoms in CI

```
1) Should complete the UM checkout form with manual gateway:
   AssertionError: Timed out retrying after 60000ms:
   expected 'http://localhost:8889/register/' to include 'status=done'
   at Context.eval (010-manual-checkout-flow.spec.js:85:29)

2) Should verify checkout state via WP-CLI:
   AssertionError: expected 'no-payments' to equal 'pending'
   at Context.eval (010-manual-checkout-flow.spec.js:95:38)
```

Both 8.1-chrome and 8.2-chrome matrix jobs fail identically. Example failed run: https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite/actions/runs/26653280713

## Suspected root cause

The spec's neighbour `020-free-trial-flow.spec.js` runs in the same job, after the same fixtures, and **passes** — so `/register/` is not broken. The difference is the **manual gateway path** specifically.

`tests/e2e/cypress/fixtures/setup-product.php` creates `Test Plan` without setting `recurring`:

```php
$product = new WP_Ultimo\Models\Product();
$product->set_name('Test Plan');
$product->set_slug('test-plan');
$product->set_amount(29.99);
$product->set_duration(1);
$product->set_duration_unit('month');
$product->set_type('plan');
$product->set_active(true);
$product->save();
```

`inc/models/class-product.php:164` declares `protected $recurring = 1;`, so `Test Plan` ends up **recurring**. `inc/gateways/class-manual-gateway.php` declares:

```php
public function supports_recurring(): bool {
    return false;
}
```

When the active plan is recurring, the manual gateway is filtered out of the gateway picker → the test's `'input[type="radio"][name="gateway"][value="manual"]'` check is gracefully skipped → the form submits without a recurring-capable gateway selected → the checkout request is rejected and the page stays on `/register/`.

This needs to be confirmed against the actual screenshot/video (currently lost in CI — see "Repro & artifact-capture caveats" below).

## Likely fixes (try in order)

### Fix 1 — make Test Plan one-time

Edit `tests/e2e/cypress/fixtures/setup-product.php`:

```php
$product->set_recurring(false);
$product->set_pricing_type('paid');
```

This makes Test Plan a one-time purchase, which the manual gateway supports. Lowest-risk change; matches the spec's intent.

### Fix 2 — pin spec to a non-recurring plan

If Fix 1 breaks other specs that need Test Plan to be recurring, instead create a dedicated `setup-manual-plan.php` fixture (mirroring `setup-trial-product.php`) and have 010 call it from its `before()` hook. Then select that plan by name in the spec.

The plan-selection change has already been made in commit `64699472` — 010 now uses `cy.contains("Test Plan")` instead of `.first()`. This is good hygiene regardless of how the recurring issue is fixed.

### Fix 3 — capture diagnostics first

If neither of the above clears the failure, set `trashAssetsBeforeRuns: false` in `cypress.config.test.js` so 010's screenshot/video survive the subsequent `npx cypress run` invocations and can be inspected from the GitHub Actions artifact.

## Files to modify

- **Primary:** `tests/e2e/cypress/fixtures/setup-product.php` — add `set_recurring(false)` and `set_pricing_type('paid')`.
- **Re-enable in CI:** `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` (step "Run Checkout Tests (After Setup)", around line 320) — add `010-manual-checkout-flow.spec.js` back to `CHECKOUT_TESTS` and remove the `TODO(#NNN)` block above it.
- **(Possibly):** `tests/e2e/cypress/integration/010-manual-checkout-flow.spec.js` — already uses `.contains("Test Plan")` after commit `64699472`. No further change should be needed.

## Reference patterns

- `tests/e2e/cypress/integration/020-free-trial-flow.spec.js` — the working sibling spec. Pattern to mirror: create the plan in `before()` with explicit `set_recurring()`/`set_pricing_type()`, select by name with `.contains()`, then submit.
- `tests/e2e/cypress/fixtures/setup-trial-product.php` — clean fixture pattern for plan creation.
- `inc/gateways/class-manual-gateway.php` (`supports_recurring()` returns `false`).
- `inc/gateways/class-base-gateway.php` — search for where `supports_recurring()` is consulted during gateway-availability filtering.
- `inc/models/class-product.php` lines 140 / 164 / 230 — defaults for `pricing_type`, `recurring`, `list_order`.

## Verification

After applying the fix:

```bash
# Re-add 010 to CHECKOUT_TESTS in .github/workflows/e2e.yml (remove TODO).

# Local — if wp-env is available:
npx cypress run \
  --config-file cypress.config.test.js \
  --spec "tests/e2e/cypress/integration/010-manual-checkout-flow.spec.js" \
  --browser chrome

# CI — push and confirm both matrix jobs pass:
#   - cypress (8.1, chrome)
#   - cypress (8.2, chrome)
```

Both `it()` blocks must pass: redirect to `status=done`, and `verify-manual-checkout-results.php` must return `um_payment_status: 'pending'`, `um_payment_gateway: 'manual'`, `um_membership_status: 'pending'`.

## Repro & artifact-capture caveats

`cypress.config.test.js` sets `trashAssetsBeforeRuns: true`. The workflow runs 010 then 020 as separate `npx cypress run` invocations in the same step — 020's run trashes 010's screenshots/videos, so the uploaded `cypress-videos-*-chrome` artifact only contains `020-free-trial-flow.spec.js.mp4`. If you need to inspect 010's UI state, either:

1. Toggle `trashAssetsBeforeRuns: false` in `cypress.config.test.js` for the diagnostic run.
2. Or split the workflow step so artifacts upload between 010 and 020.

## Why this happened (PR #1280 context)

PR #1280 added 9 cypress specs to the workflow that "existed but were never invoked". 010 was one of them — it had no green CI baseline, just a green developer machine. The recurring-default mismatch with the manual gateway only surfaces in real form submission, not in the unit tests.

The blocked PR that surfaced this: #1316 (Sender BCC + wp_mail Throwable guard). PR #1316's diff is unrelated to checkout, gateways, or e2e — only the workflow-level failure overlap blocked it.

title: test(e2e): restore cross-domain SSO Cypress spec once wp-env supports mapped non-standard ports
body:
## Restore `tests/e2e/cypress/integration/060-sso-cross-domain.spec.js`

The cross-domain SSO Cypress spec (added in `b232e296`, Feb 16 2026) has never passed on `main`. It was just skipped in PR (linked below) to unblock the required `cypress (8.2, chrome)` status check. The SSO trigger logic that does work in the current env is already covered by `065-sso-redirect-loop.spec.js` (passing).

## Root cause (environment, not product)

The spec uses `localhost:8889` for the main site and `127.0.0.1:8889` for the mapped subsite domain. In the wp-env Docker setup (port 8889) Ultimate Multisite's domain mapping does not take effect for the mapped host on a non-standard port: requests to `http://127.0.0.1:8889/` are 302-redirected back to `http://localhost:8889/`. The spec's own header note even acknowledges this ("the SSO redirect chain goes through localhost:8889 where cookies already exist"), but the assertions were still written as if the mapping worked end-to-end. Failing assertions on every run:

- `expect(response.status).to.eq(200)` for `http://127.0.0.1:8889/` — gets 302
- `expect(response.headers.location).to.include('sso=login')` — never reached
- `cy.url().should('include', '/wp-admin/')` (timeout 60 s) — final URL stays on `http://localhost:8889/`
- Same as above for the `redirect_to` preservation test

## Options to restore (pick one)

1. **Run wp-env on port 80** (`.wp-env.json` / `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`) so WordPress strips the port and the mapped host matches normally. Risk: port 80 collisions with other CI services.
2. **Add a host alias** (`/etc/hosts`-style entry inside the wp-env containers) so a second hostname like `mapped.test:8889` resolves to the same wp container and the domain mapping is inserted for that exact `host:port` pair.
3. **Reverse-proxy via Caddy/Traefik** in front of the wp-env container so the mapped hostname terminates on standard ports while the underlying wp keeps :8889.
4. **Drop the spec entirely** if cross-domain SSO is considered adequately covered by `065-sso-redirect-loop.spec.js` plus the PHPUnit SSO suite under `tests/WP_Ultimo/SSO/`.

## Files to touch

- `tests/e2e/cypress/integration/060-sso-cross-domain.spec.js` — remove `describe.skip(...)` and the FIXME block once the env is fixed.
- `tests/e2e/cypress/fixtures/setup-sso-test.php` — likely no change unless the chosen approach changes the mapped host string.
- `.wp-env.json` and/or `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` — env reconfiguration for options 1–3.

## Reference pattern

`tests/e2e/cypress/integration/065-sso-redirect-loop.spec.js` already exercises the SSO trigger logic that works on the current env (6/6 passing). Mirror its setup approach for any new assertions.

## Verification

After re-enabling, run locally with `npm run cy:run:chrome -- --spec tests/e2e/cypress/integration/060-sso-cross-domain.spec.js` (requires Docker + wp-env) and then via the `E2E Tests` GitHub Actions workflow on a PR. All four tests in the describe block must pass without `.skip`.

title: Prevent duplicate main plugin folders from crashing sunrise loader
body:
## Goal
Prevent a critical-error class of failures when a duplicate Ultimate Multisite main plugin directory is present under a name that matches the addon sunrise glob pattern.

## Production symptom observed
A WordPress multisite went HTTP 500 immediately after uploading/installing the latest main Ultimate Multisite build into a duplicate plugin directory such as:

```text
wp-content/plugins/ultimate-multisite-1-1
```

Fatal error pattern:

```text
Cannot redeclare wu_remove_sunrise_warning()
previously declared in wp-content/sunrise.php:80
redeclared in wp-content/plugins/ultimate-multisite-1-1/sunrise.php:80
```

Recovery was to move the duplicate folder out of the `ultimate-multisite-*` namespace so the sunrise addon loader stopped loading its `sunrise.php` as an addon sunrise file. The canonical `ultimate-multisite` plugin remained network-active and the site returned HTTP 200.

## Likely cause
`WP_Ultimo\Sunrise` discovers addon sunrise files using a broad pattern:

```php
plugins/ultimate-multisite-*/sunrise.php
```

Reference path/pattern:

- `inc/class-sunrise.php`: addon sunrise discovery/loader around the `glob( $plugins_dir . '/ultimate-multisite-*/sunrise.php' )` pattern.
- `sunrise.php`: defines `wu_remove_sunrise_warning()`.
- `ultimate-multisite.php`: copies the main plugin `sunrise.php` into `wp-content/sunrise.php` when present.

A failed/duplicate WordPress upload can create `ultimate-multisite-1`, `ultimate-multisite-1-1`, etc. Those are duplicate main plugin folders, not addons, but they match `ultimate-multisite-*`. The loader then includes the duplicate main plugin's `sunrise.php`, which redeclares functions already loaded from `wp-content/sunrise.php`.

## Worker-ready implementation options
Choose the least invasive robust fix:

1. In `inc/class-sunrise.php`, filter addon sunrise candidates so the main plugin's duplicate folders are ignored.
   - Exclude candidates whose directory contains the main plugin bootstrap `ultimate-multisite.php`.
   - Or exclude candidates whose basename matches duplicate-main patterns such as `ultimate-multisite-1`, `ultimate-multisite-1-1`, etc.
   - Prefer the bootstrap-file exclusion because it detects duplicate main packages regardless of exact suffix.
2. Add a defensive `function_exists( 'wu_remove_sunrise_warning' )` guard in root `sunrise.php` only if needed, but do not rely on this alone if loading duplicate main sunrise files can cause other duplicated side effects.
3. Keep legitimate addon sunrise files loading, e.g. `ultimate-multisite-woocommerce/sunrise.php` and `ultimate-multisite-support-agents/sunrise.php`.

## Acceptance criteria
- A duplicate main plugin directory named `wp-content/plugins/ultimate-multisite-1-1` with its own `sunrise.php` does not cause a fatal error during sunrise loading.
- Legitimate addon sunrise files in `wp-content/plugins/ultimate-multisite-{addon}/sunrise.php` still load.
- The loader does not include a candidate directory that contains `ultimate-multisite.php` as a main plugin bootstrap duplicate.
- No public warnings or admin notices regress when the canonical `wp-content/sunrise.php` is present.

## Suggested tests
Add/adjust tests around the sunrise addon discovery method if feasible:

1. Create fixture/plugin dirs:
   - `ultimate-multisite/sunrise.php` canonical main plugin directory.
   - `ultimate-multisite-1-1/sunrise.php` plus `ultimate-multisite-1-1/ultimate-multisite.php` duplicate main plugin.
   - `ultimate-multisite-woocommerce/sunrise.php` legitimate addon.
2. Assert discovery excludes `ultimate-multisite-1-1/sunrise.php`.
3. Assert discovery includes `ultimate-multisite-woocommerce/sunrise.php`.
4. Run the existing PHP test suite or targeted sunrise tests.

## Verification commands
Use the repo's normal checks, for example:

```bash
vendor/bin/phpunit --filter Sunrise
vendor/bin/phpcs
```

If no sunrise test harness exists, add a focused unit test for the candidate filtering logic and run the closest available PHPUnit target.

title: bug: Ultimate Multisite list-table search drops page query and breaks row actions
body:
## Summary

Ultimate Multisite list-table search updates the browser URL without preserving the admin `page` query argument. After searching, row actions stop navigating even though their `href` values are correct.

## Baseline

- Branch: `main`
- Commit tested: `0b7fe4e0`
- Reproduced in Network Admin with only the target plugin and non-UM dependencies active.

## Browser evidence

Reproduced on:

- Products
- Memberships
- Customers

Example on Products:

1. Open `/wp-admin/network/admin.php?page=wp-ultimo-products&main_retest=0b7fe4e0`.
2. Search for `Test Plan`.
3. URL becomes:

```text
/wp-admin/network/admin.php?paged=1&s=Test%20Plan
```

Expected URL should preserve:

```text
page=wp-ultimo-products
```

After the URL drops `page`, clicking row actions such as Edit/Manage does not navigate, even though the anchor `href` points at the correct edit URL.

## Suspected files / patterns

- `assets/js/list-tables.js` — history update / AJAX form data handling.
- `assets/js/list-tables.min.js` — generated asset parity.
- List admin page/table classes that depend on `page` during AJAX/search navigation.

Likely pattern: the `history.pushState` data is derived from list-table form data and does not include the current `page` argument.

## Acceptance criteria

- Searching list tables preserves the current `page=wp-ultimo-*` parameter.
- Row actions still navigate after a search/filter/pagination interaction.
- Products, Memberships, Customers, and other Ultimate Multisite list pages behave consistently.

## Suggested verification

Manual browser-agent checks:

1. Products: search `Test Plan`; confirm URL includes `page=wp-ultimo-products`; click Edit.
2. Memberships: search `schaucr`; confirm URL includes `page=wp-ultimo-memberships`; click Edit.
3. Customers: search `schaucr`; confirm URL includes `page=wp-ultimo-customers`; click Manage.

```bash
npm run lint:js
```

Delete confirmation modals can render correctly, but submitting them from model edit pages does not delete the target record. This is separate from #1344, where the Product delete modal endpoint returns `0` instead of rendering the confirmation UI.

## Evidence

Validated in the network admin browser session on current `main` (`0b7fe4e0`):

- Site edit page: created disposable Site ID 35, opened `DELETE SITE` modal, submitted it, then `wu_get_site(35)` still returned the site. Cleaned up with `$site->delete()`.
- Domain edit page: created disposable Domain ID 9, opened `DELETE DOMAIN` modal, submitted it, then `wu_get_domain(9)` still returned the domain. Cleaned up with `$domain->delete()`.
- Discount Code edit page: created disposable Discount Code ID 2, opened `DELETE DISCOUNT CODE` modal, submitted it, then `wu_get_discount_code(2)` still returned the code. Cleaned up with `$discount_code->delete()`.
- Broadcast edit page: created disposable Broadcast ID 21, opened `DELETE BROADCAST` modal, submitted it with `form.requestSubmit(...)`, then `wu_get_broadcast(21)` still returned the broadcast. Cleaned up with `$broadcast->delete()`.

The modal UI itself rendered for these models with hidden fields like `id`, `model`, `action=wu_form_handler`, and a `DELETE` submit button. The submit attempt stayed on the edit URL and did not remove the model.

## Expected

Submitting a rendered delete confirmation modal should delete the target model and redirect back to the relevant list/admin page, or show an actionable error if deletion is blocked.

## Actual

The confirmation modal renders, but submit does not delete the model. Data-layer verification confirms the records remain.

## Likely files/patterns

- `inc/managers/class-form-manager.php` — registers/renders `delete_modal` and handles `wu_ajax_wu_form_handler`.
- `inc/admin-pages/class-edit-admin-page.php` — edit-page delete modal link generation.
- Model list tables also generate `delete_modal` row actions, e.g. `inc/list-tables/class-domain-list-table.php`, `inc/list-tables/class-discount-code-list-table.php`, `inc/list-tables/class-broadcast-list-table.php`, `inc/list-tables/class-site-list-table.php`.

## Verification

After fixing, verify with at least one cheap disposable model and one edit-page delete flow:

1. Create a disposable Discount Code.
2. Open its edit page.
3. Click `DELETE DISCOUNT CODE`.
4. Confirm deletion in the modal.
5. Assert `wu_get_discount_code($id)` returns false.
6. Repeat one non-discount model if the fix touches shared modal handling.

Also keep #1344 separate: Product currently fails earlier because its delete modal endpoint returns `0` instead of rendering the confirmation modal.

> 
> 💡 Result:
> 
> Yes, PHP's SplFileInfo::getRealPath resolves all symbolic links [1][2]. It expands symlinks, resolves relative references (like /./ or /../), and returns the canonicalized absolute path to the file [3][2]. If the file does not exist, the method returns false [1][2]. title: Complete OCI transactional email domain setup
body:
## Summary

Complete the OCI Email Delivery provider so it is production-ready for mixed mailbox-provider + OCI transactional email setups.

## Context

The current OCI provider can create/list Email Delivery domains and emit DNS records, but local testing found these gaps:

- The OCI Email Delivery control-plane endpoint must use `https://ctrl.email.{region}.oci.oraclecloud.com/20170907/`.
- DKIM list responses do not include the DNS target values; the provider must fetch DKIM details after create/list before building DNS records.
- A transactional sender address such as `support@example.com` should be provisioned/verified as an OCI approved sender idempotently.
- Mixed mailbox-provider setups need existing MX/mailbox-provider records preserved while OCI manages only transactional auth records.

## Files / areas to inspect

- `inc/integrations/providers/oci-email/class-oci-email-integration.php`
- `inc/integrations/providers/oci-email/class-oci-email-transactional-email.php`
- `inc/integrations/capabilities/interface-transactional-email-capability.php`
- Existing SES reference: `inc/integrations/providers/amazon-ses/class-amazon-ses-transactional-email.php`

## Implementation requirements

1. Use the OCI Email Delivery control-plane endpoint by default:
   - `https://ctrl.email.{region}.oci.oraclecloud.com/20170907/`
   - Preserve the existing endpoint override setting.
2. When building DKIM DNS records:
   - if an existing DKIM is returned by list, call the DKIM detail endpoint before extracting DNS fields;
   - if a DKIM is newly created, wait/poll or fetch details until DNS fields are available;
   - support OCI response fields for CNAME and TXT DKIM formats.
3. Add idempotent approved sender management:
   - configurable default local part, e.g. `support` or `info`;
   - create sender only if it does not already exist;
   - return clear status/errors when sender creation fails.
4. Keep outbound sending behavior unchanged for OCI:
   - WordPress sends through the configured SMTP/msmtp transport;
   - the integration manages OCI domains, DKIM, SPF guidance, and approved senders.
5. Log domain/sender/DKIM actions with provider-specific context and no secrets.

## Acceptance criteria

- `verify_domain('example.com')` is idempotent and returns SPF + DKIM + DMARC records with complete DNS values.
- Existing OCI email domains and DKIMs are reused, not duplicated.
- An approved sender can be created/reused for the configured local part.
- Connection tests still pass with stored credentials and wp-config constants.
- No secrets or private key material are logged or returned.

## Verification

Run targeted checks:

```bash
php -l inc/integrations/providers/oci-email/class-oci-email-integration.php
php -l inc/integrations/providers/oci-email/class-oci-email-transactional-email.php
```


Expected: returned records include a non-empty OCI DKIM target.

title: Publish transactional email DNS records via Cloudflare
body:
## Summary

Add automatic Cloudflare DNS publication for transactional email authentication records emitted by OCI/SES integrations.

## Context

Transactional email providers emit SPF/DKIM/DMARC records, but the Cloudflare integration currently focuses on domain mapping/subdomain records and Custom Hostnames. It does not consume `wu_domain_verified` DNS records and publish them. This prevents end-to-end automatic setup for multisite domains.

Mixed mailbox-provider + OCI use case:

- mailbox provider keeps MX, mailbox DKIM, ownership, and existing DMARC;
- OCI handles WordPress/WooCommerce transactional sending;
- SPF must be merged into a single TXT record;
- OCI DKIM CNAME/TXT must be added unproxied;
- existing Purelymail/Google/Microsoft/etc. records must not be removed.

## Files / areas to inspect

- `inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-integration.php`
- `inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php`
- `inc/integrations/providers/oci-email/class-oci-email-transactional-email.php`
- `inc/integrations/providers/amazon-ses/class-amazon-ses-transactional-email.php`
- `inc/managers/class-domain-manager.php` around `wu_domain_added` / `wu_domain_verified`
- DNS management references: `inc/managers/class-dns-record-manager.php`

## Implementation requirements

1. Add a Cloudflare handler for transactional email DNS records:
   - listen to `wu_domain_verified` or introduce a provider-neutral hook if needed;
   - accept records shaped like `type`, `name`, `value`.
2. Implement Cloudflare zone discovery:
   - choose the longest matching active Cloudflare zone for the domain;
   - support apex domains and subdomains;
   - log and skip when no zone is accessible.
3. Implement safe DNS upserts:
   - SPF: merge `include:` mechanisms into the single existing SPF TXT record;
   - never create duplicate SPF records;
   - DKIM: create/update CNAME or TXT records, unproxied;
   - DMARC: preserve an existing DMARC TXT/CNAME by default;
   - create default DMARC only when none exists and the transactional provider supplies one.
4. Add settings/filters:
   - enable/disable automatic transactional DNS publication;
   - preserve existing DMARC (default true);
   - allow mailbox-provider SPF includes to be preserved;
   - expose filters for record normalization and skip rules.
5. Add clear logging:
   - created/updated/skipped records;
   - zone selection;
   - reasons for skipped records.

## Acceptance criteria

- When a domain is verified by OCI/SES, Cloudflare automatically publishes the required auth records if the zone is accessible.
- Existing mailbox-provider MX/DKIM/ownership records remain unchanged.
- Existing SPF is updated in-place to include the transactional provider include.
- Existing DMARC CNAME/TXT is preserved unless explicitly configured otherwise.
- Missing zones are skipped with actionable logs, not fatal errors.

## Verification

Run targeted checks:

```bash
php -l inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-integration.php
php -l inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php
vendor/bin/phpcs inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-integration.php inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php
```

In a dev WordPress install with Cloudflare + OCI credentials configured:

```bash
wp eval 'do_action("wu_domain_verified", "example.com", 1, [["type"=>"TXT", "name"=>"example.com", "value"=>"v=spf1 include:rp.oracleemaildelivery.com ~all"]]);'
```

Expected: Cloudflare has a single SPF record with the new include merged.

title: fix: stop idle import cron polling across all sites
body:
## Summary

`wu_import_network` and `wu_import_site` are being scheduled and executed once per minute across many multisite subsites even when no import is pending. This creates unnecessary WP-Cron / queue worker load and obscures real queue activity.

## Evidence

Observed on a production multisite after the queue worker deploy:

- Last 2 hours: `wu_import_network` executed 1,961 times.
- Last 2 hours: `wu_import_site` executed 1,944 times.
- Pending import transients across the network: 0.
- The events were scheduled on most sites with recurrence `wu_site_every_minute` and empty args.

Relevant code:

- `inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php`
  - `maybe_run_imports()` runs on `init`.
  - It schedules `wu_import_site` with `wu_site_every_minute` whenever `wp_next_scheduled( 'wu_import_site' )` is false.
  - It schedules `wu_import_network` with `wu_site_every_minute` whenever `wp_next_scheduled( 'wu_import_network' )` is false.
  - There is no pending-import guard at schedule time.
- `inc/functions/importer.php`
  - `wu_exporter_add_pending_import()` writes `wu_pending_site_import_*` transient data.
  - `wu_exporter_add_pending_network_import()` writes `wu_pending_network_import_*` transient data.
  - `wu_exporter_get_pending_imports()` and `wu_exporter_get_pending_network_imports()` already expose pending-import state.

## Expected behavior

The import cron hooks should not poll every minute across all sites when there is no import to process.

## Recommended implementation

1. Change `Site_Exporter::maybe_run_imports()` in `inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php` so it schedules:
   - `wu_import_site` only when `wu_exporter_get_pending_imports()` is non-empty.
   - `wu_import_network` only when `wu_exporter_get_pending_network_imports()` is non-empty.
2. Ensure the custom `wu_site_every_minute` interval remains registered independently so scheduling still succeeds when a pending import is created.
3. Add explicit scheduling at import enqueue time if needed:
   - after `wu_exporter_set_transient( "wu_pending_site_import_{$hash}", ... )` in `wu_exporter_add_pending_import()`;
   - after `wu_exporter_set_transient( "wu_pending_network_import_{$hash}", ... )` in `wu_exporter_add_pending_network_import()`.
4. Add tests covering:
   - no pending imports → neither import event is scheduled by `maybe_run_imports()`;
   - pending site import → `wu_import_site` is scheduled;
   - pending network import → `wu_import_network` is scheduled;
   - enqueue helpers schedule or trigger scheduling for their corresponding hook.

## Production cleanup after merge/deploy

After the fix is deployed, unschedule existing idle events only when there are no pending imports:

```bash
wp eval '
foreach ( get_sites( [ "number" => 0, "fields" => "ids" ] ) as $blog_id ) {
    switch_to_blog( $blog_id );
    foreach ( [ "wu_import_site", "wu_import_network" ] as $hook ) {
        while ( $timestamp = wp_next_scheduled( $hook ) ) {
            wp_unschedule_event( $timestamp, $hook );
        }
    }
    restore_current_blog();
}
'
```

Only run cleanup after confirming both pending import collections are empty.

## Verification

- Unit/integration tests for the scheduling cases above.
- In a WP-CLI shell or test bootstrap:
  - with no pending imports, call `Site_Exporter::get_instance()->maybe_run_imports()` and assert `wp_next_scheduled( 'wu_import_site' )` and `wp_next_scheduled( 'wu_import_network' )` are false.
  - enqueue a site import and assert only `wu_import_site` is scheduled.
  - enqueue a network import and assert only `wu_import_network` is scheduled.
- On a deployed multisite, confirm queue logs no longer show thousands of idle `wu_import_network` / `wu_import_site` executions over a 1-2 hour window when no imports are pending.

## Notes for worker

This is a bug fix in Ultimate Multisite, not in the Bedrock/Trellis deployment repo. Keep the change scoped to the Ultimate Multisite plugin and tests. Do not alter queue worker concurrency or WP-Cron service settings for this issue.
